title: FortiGate Administrator Login Failure
description: A single failed login attempt against the FortiGate administrative GUI, CLI (SSH/console), or REST API. On its own this is low-severity noise (typos, expired passwords), but it is the atomic building block for the brute-force, password-spray, and successful-login-after-failures detections below. FortiGate reports this as a system event with action=login, status=failed.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrative login attempts, success/failure, source IP, interface used.

detection_logic: Filters FortiGate event log for administrative login events where status=failed.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=failed
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, ui, reason
tuning_guidance: Expect background noise from expired credentials and typos; this entry is atomic and not meant to alert on its own — use FGT-002/003 for volume-based detection.
investigation_steps: Confirm the source IP is an expected management workstation or jump host.
Check whether the same user has repeated failures across a short window (see FGT-002).
response_guidance: No action required for an isolated failure; escalate per FGT-002/003 if a pattern emerges.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated FortiGate Administrator Login Failures
description: Five or more failed administrative login attempts against the same FortiGate within 10 minutes, from one or more source IPs. Distinguishes routine typos from a sustained password-guessing attempt against the management plane.
detection_logic: Counts failed admin logins per device in a rolling window; alerts above threshold regardless of whether the source IP or username varies.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=failed
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, dc(user) as distinct_users, dc(srcip) as distinct_sources, values(srcip) as source_ips by devname, _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for devices behind a shared NAT/jump host where legitimate admins commonly mistype credentials in bursts (e.g. scripted health checks with stale credentials).
investigation_steps: Determine whether distinct_users is 1 (targeted) or many (spray, see FGT-003).
Check whether any of the attempted usernames are valid/disabled admin accounts.
Cross-reference source_ips against known management IP allowlist.
response_guidance: Temporarily block the source IP at the perimeter if external; verify no successful login followed (see FGT-004); rotate credentials for any targeted account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Password Spraying
description: A single source IP attempting authentication against many distinct FortiGate administrator usernames in a short window — the signature of password spraying, where an attacker tries one or two common passwords across a large account list to stay under per-account lockout thresholds.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrative login failures with username and source IP.

detection_logic: Counts distinct usernames attempted per source IP in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=failed
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(user) as distinct_users, values(user) as usernames_tried, count by srcip, devname, _time
| where distinct_users>=6
tuning_guidance: Vulnerability scanners and misconfigured RADIUS/LDAP proxies can also generate multi-username failures — cross-check srcip against known scanner ranges before escalating.
investigation_steps: List usernames_tried for validity against the real administrator roster.
Check whether any attempt in the window succeeded (FGT-004).
Check FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS logs if central auth is in use.
response_guidance: Block the source IP; force password reset on any valid usernames that were targeted; review MFA enforcement for all administrators.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful FortiGate Administrator Login Following Repeated Failures
description: A successful FortiGate administrative login for a user/source pair that had five or more failed attempts in the preceding 30 minutes. This is the single highest-value authentication detection in the catalogue: it means a guessing or spraying attempt against the management plane ultimately succeeded.
detection_logic: Joins a failed-login threshold search with a subsequent success for the same user or source IP within the correlation window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login
| eval outcome=if(status="failed","fail","success")
| transaction user, devname maxspan=30m startswith=eval(outcome="fail") endswith=eval(outcome="success")
| where eventcount>=6
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, eventcount
tuning_guidance: A legitimate admin who mistypes a password several times before succeeding will also match — cross-reference srcip against the known management allowlist before treating as high-confidence compromise.
investigation_steps: Confirm srcip is not a known-good management workstation.
Review every action taken by this session (config changes, policy edits) for the following hour.
Check for MFA bypass or absence.
response_guidance: Suspend the account immediately, force a password/MFA reset, and review all configuration changes made during the session; treat as a confirmed compromise until proven otherwise.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Source IP for FortiGate Administrator
description: A successful administrative login from a source IP never seen for that user in the prior 30 days. Legitimate travel, new jump hosts, or ISP changes cause this too, but it is a meaningful first-seen signal on infrastructure that should normally be administered from a fixed, small set of IPs.
detection_logic: Builds a 30-day baseline of (user, srcip) pairs and flags a successful login for a pair never seen before.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success
[ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h
  | stats count by user, srcip | fields user, srcip | format ]
| stats count by user, srcip
tuning_guidance: Best implemented as a lookup-backed baseline (nightly `| outputlookup fgt_admin_ip_baseline`) rather than the subsearch shown, which is illustrative only and will not scale past a small baseline set.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the administrator whether the new source is expected (new location, new jump host).
Check whether MFA was satisfied for the session.
Review geolocation of the new source IP.
response_guidance: If unconfirmed, treat as potential account compromise: suspend session, verify recent config changes, force credential rotation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Login Outside Management Network
description: A successful administrative login whose source IP falls outside the CIDR ranges of the designated out-of-band/jump-host management network. FortiGate management access should be restricted by trusted-hosts configuration (see FGT-016) and this detects a login that either bypassed that control or occurred on an interface that should never expose admin access.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrative login events with source IP and interface.

detection_logic: Compares login source IP against a maintained lookup of approved management CIDR ranges; flags anything outside it.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success
| lookup fgt_management_cidrs.csv srcip OUTPUT is_management_range
| where isnull(is_management_range)
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, ui
tuning_guidance: Maintain fgt_management_cidrs.csv as a curated allowlist; review quarterly as jump-host ranges change. Exclude known VPN pools used for legitimate remote administration if applicable.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether trusted-hosts restrictions are configured on the admin account (FGT-016 gap).
Determine if the interface used (ui field) is the WAN interface — a direct signal of an exposed management plane.
response_guidance: If the login originated on a WAN-facing interface, treat as Critical and assume the management interface is Internet-exposed; restrict immediately and audit all recent changes.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Login Outside Business Hours
description: A successful administrative login occurring outside the organization's defined change/maintenance hours. Not inherently malicious — on-call response is legitimate — but combined with other signals (new source, config changes) it raises confidence of unauthorized access.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrative login success events with timestamp.

detection_logic: Flags successful logins whose hour-of-day/day-of-week falls outside a configured business-hours window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H"), dow=strftime(_time,"%a")
| where (hour<"06" OR hour>="20") OR dow=="Sat" OR dow=="Sun"
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, hour, dow
tuning_guidance: Tune the business-hours window per organization and time zone; exclude known on-call rotations or automation service accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the administrator whether this was a planned change or incident response.
Check for any configuration changes made during the session.
response_guidance: No automatic action; use as a contributing signal in higher-confidence correlations (FGT-020 defense-evasion sequence).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Disabled FortiGate Administrator Login Attempt
description: A login attempt (successful or failed) using an administrator account that is currently disabled in the FortiGate configuration. A successful login on a disabled account is a strong indicator that the account status was silently re-enabled or that authentication is bypassing the local account-status check (e.g. via a remote-auth fallback misconfiguration).

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Login events cross-referenced with current administrator account status.

detection_logic: Joins login events against a maintained lookup of currently-disabled administrator accounts.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login
| lookup fgt_disabled_admins.csv user OUTPUT is_disabled
| where is_disabled="true"
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, status
tuning_guidance: Requires a scheduled search or config-export job to keep fgt_disabled_admins.csv current; stale lookups will miss recently-disabled accounts.
investigation_steps: Verify current account status directly on the FortiGate.
If the login succeeded, this is a critical finding — investigate immediately.
response_guidance: Treat a successful login on a disabled account as a confirmed security incident: isolate the device from remote management, audit the full admin account list for tampering.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Local FortiGate Administrator Login When Centralized Authentication Expected
description: A successful login using a local FortiGate administrator account in an environment where RADIUS/LDAP/FortiAuthenticator-backed centralized authentication is the expected mechanism. Local accounts frequently exist as break-glass credentials; use of one outside a declared emergency is a signal that centralized authentication (and its logging/MFA) is being deliberately bypassed.
detection_logic: Flags successful logins where authserver is empty/local while a lookup of expected-remote-auth admin accounts marks the user as centrally managed.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success
| lookup fgt_centralized_admins.csv user OUTPUT expects_remote_auth
| where expects_remote_auth="true" AND (isnull(authserver) OR authserver="")
| table _time, devname, user, srcip
tuning_guidance: Explicitly allowlist declared break-glass accounts and known DR/console-only scenarios where local auth is intentional.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether this matches a declared break-glass procedure/change ticket.
Check whether FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS was reachable at the time (legitimate fallback) vs. deliberately bypassed.
response_guidance: If unconfirmed, treat as a defense-evasion attempt to avoid centralized MFA/logging; rotate the local account credential and review its trusted-hosts restriction.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Emergency/Break-Glass Administrator Account Used
description: A login using an account explicitly designated as an emergency/break-glass credential (typically a default or rarely-used local super-admin kept for DR scenarios). Any use of this account outside a declared incident/change window warrants immediate review — it is one of the highest-value credentials on the device by design.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Login events for a maintained list of break-glass account names.

detection_logic: Matches login events (success or failure) against a curated list of break-glass account usernames.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login
| lookup fgt_breakglass_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_breakglass
| where is_breakglass="true"
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, status
tuning_guidance: Suppress only for a pre-declared change ticket/incident window with an explicit start/end time recorded in a lookup, not a blanket exclusion.
investigation_steps: Verify against the change-management system whether use was pre-approved.
Review every action taken during the session.
response_guidance: If not pre-approved, treat as Critical: assume compromise, rotate the break-glass credential immediately, and audit all configuration changes made during the session.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Console Administrator Login
description: An administrative login via the physical/serial console port. Console access implies physical proximity (or access to a console server/KVM), so it is rarer and higher-signal than network-based administration in most environments.
detection_logic: Filters admin login events where the interface field indicates console access.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success ui="console"
| table _time, devname, user
tuning_guidance: Expected during scheduled physical maintenance or when reachable via a console server (e.g. Opengear, iDRAC-attached serial) — cross-reference with a maintenance calendar if one exists.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether physical/console-server access was scheduled or authorized.
If the environment uses a console server, correlate with its own access logs.
response_guidance: If unexpected, treat as a potential physical-security or console-server compromise incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate SSH Administrator Login
description: An administrative login via SSH. Tracked separately from HTTPS/GUI logins because SSH sessions run raw CLI commands that are individually less visible in structured logs than GUI-driven config changes, and because SSH key-based auth (if enabled) bypasses password/MFA controls entirely.
detection_logic: Filters admin login events for SSH interface.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success ui="ssh(login)"
| table _time, devname, user, srcip
tuning_guidance: Baseline is essential — most environments have a small set of known SSH admin sources (Ansible/automation, jump hosts).
investigation_steps: Cross-reference srcip against the automation/jump-host allowlist.
If SSH key auth is enabled, verify which key fingerprint authenticated (requires verbose SSH logging if available).
response_guidance: No automatic action for expected sources; investigate as FGT-006 if srcip is outside the management network.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate HTTPS/GUI Administrator Login
description: An administrative login via the HTTPS management GUI. The baseline detection for GUI-driven configuration sessions; most of the FortiGate configuration-change detections in this catalogue (FGT-020 onward) are downstream of a session that starts here.
detection_logic: Filters admin login events for the HTTPS GUI interface.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success ui="https(login)"
| table _time, devname, user, srcip
tuning_guidance: High-volume, expected event — not an alert by itself; used as the anchor event for sequence detections.
investigation_steps: N/A for isolated events — see downstream sequence detections.
response_guidance: N/A — informational baseline event.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator MFA Not Satisfied on Login
description: A successful administrative login recorded without a corresponding two-factor/FortiToken authentication event, for an account that is configured to require MFA. Indicates either an MFA-bypass path (e.g. API/token-based auth that skips the interactive 2FA prompt) or that MFA enforcement was recently disabled for the account (see FGT-018).

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Login success events cross-referenced with two-factor completion status.

detection_logic: Joins successful logins against a lookup of accounts configured to require 2FA and flags sessions lacking a two-factor completion marker.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action=login status=success
| lookup fgt_mfa_required_admins.csv user OUTPUT mfa_required
| where mfa_required="true" AND NOT (msg="*two-factor*" OR msg="*token*")
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, msg
tuning_guidance: Verify actual FortiOS log field/message text against your firmware version for two-factor completion — the msg-string match shown is illustrative and version-dependent.
investigation_steps: Confirm MFA/FortiToken configuration is still active for this account (FGT-018).
Check the authentication method used (API token vs. interactive).
response_guidance: If MFA was bypassed unexpectedly, treat the session as high-risk: review all changes made and re-enforce MFA immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator API Token Authentication
description: A REST API session authenticated with a static API token rather than an interactive username/password/MFA session. API tokens are powerful (they can carry the same privilege as the admin profile they're bound to) and typically bypass interactive MFA — track their use as its own category.
detection_logic: Filters login/session events for API-token-based authentication.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (ui="*api*" OR msg="*API*token*")
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, msg
tuning_guidance: Baseline expected automation source IPs (CI/CD, orchestration tools) and alert only on new/unexpected sources.
investigation_steps: Confirm the token belongs to a known automation integration.
Check the scope/profile bound to the token.
response_guidance: Revoke and reissue any token used from an unexpected source; review token expiry policy.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Trusted Hosts Restriction Removed or Weakened
description: An administrator account's `trusted-hosts` restriction — which limits which source IPs/subnets may even attempt to authenticate as that account — is removed or broadened to 0.0.0.0/0. This is one of the most consequential single configuration changes on a FortiGate: it turns a scoped management surface into one reachable from anywhere the interface is exposed.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrator object configuration changes, specifically the trusted-hosts attribute.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events on the system.admin object where the changed attribute is trusthost and the new value is broadened.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.admin" cfgattr="*trusthost*"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning expected — this should be a rare, deliberate, change-ticket-backed action; treat any unticketed occurrence as high-priority.
investigation_steps: Identify who made the change and cross-reference against a change ticket.
Check whether this correlates with a subsequent login from a new source IP (FGT-005/FGT-006).
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized; audit all administrator accounts for similarly weakened trusted-hosts settings.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Idle Timeout Weakened
description: The global administrator idle-timeout setting is increased or disabled, extending how long an authenticated management session remains active without interaction. Attackers who have hijacked an admin session (e.g. via an unattended, unlocked workstation) benefit from a longer window.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Global system configuration changes to admintimeout.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events where the changed attribute is admintimeout and the new value increases the session lifetime.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.global" cfgattr="admintimeout"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for troubleshooting long-running console operations; require a change ticket for any permanent increase.
investigation_steps: Determine whether the change was reverted after a maintenance window.
response_guidance: Revert to the organizational standard timeout if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Two-Factor Authentication Disabled
description: Two-factor/FortiToken authentication is disabled for one or more administrator accounts. This directly removes a control that protects against exactly the credential-guessing and phishing scenarios detected elsewhere in this catalogue (FGT-002/003/004), and is a common step for an attacker consolidating access after an initial compromise.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrator object changes to the two-factor attribute.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events on system.admin where the two-factor attribute is changed to disabled.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.admin" cfgattr="two-factor"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate pattern expected outside a documented account-recovery procedure — treat every occurrence as requiring explicit justification.
investigation_steps: Identify who disabled MFA and for which account.
Check whether the target account subsequently logged in (FGT-014).
response_guidance: Re-enable MFA immediately unless explicitly authorized; treat the acting administrator's own session as suspect and review their recent activity.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Remote Authentication Server Configuration Changed
description: The RADIUS, LDAP, or FortiAuthenticator server configuration used for centralized administrator authentication is modified — server address, shared secret, or query filter. An attacker who controls this configuration can point authentication at a rogue server they control, effectively creating an authentication backdoor.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events on user.radius/user.ldap objects for server address or secret changes.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="user.radius" OR cfgpath="user.ldap") (cfgattr="server" OR cfgattr="secret" OR cfgattr="*key*")
| table _time, devname, user, cfgpath, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned identity-infrastructure migrations; require a change ticket for the server-address attribute in particular.
investigation_steps: Verify the new server address/IP is a known, owned authentication server.
Check for any subsequent successful admin logins that may now be authenticating against a rogue server.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately; audit all administrator logins since the change for validity.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Admin Login Followed by New Super-Admin and Logging Disabled
description: The management-plane-compromise sequence prioritized by the master specification: an administrative login is followed, within the same session window, by creation of a new super-admin account and a weakening of logging/security-profile settings. Individually each step has a legitimate use; the sequence is the highest-confidence indicator of a compromised or malicious insider administrative session in this catalogue.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Login, administrator-creation, and logging-configuration events correlated by session/user.

detection_logic: Correlates three event classes for the same acting administrator within a 20-minute window: login success, system.admin create with accprofile=super_admin, and a logging/security-profile weakening change.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system
| eval stage=case(action="login" AND status="success","1_login", cfgpath="system.admin" AND action="Add" AND cfgattr="*super_admin*","2_new_superadmin", (cfgattr="*log*" OR cfgattr="*ips*" OR cfgattr="*av*") AND action="Edit","3_control_weakened", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=20m startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a well-defined 'control weakening' keyword set tuned to your FortiOS version's cfgattr naming; validate against real config-change logs before enabling as a page-worthy alert.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident: identify the new super-admin account and disable it.
Restore logging/security-profile settings.
Review every action taken by the originating session.
response_guidance: Isolate the FortiGate from remote management, disable the new account, restore configuration from known-good backup, and initiate incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: login -> new super_admin -> control weakened, same user

title: New FortiGate Administrator Account Created
description: A new local administrator account is created on the FortiGate. Legitimate during onboarding or automation setup, but also the single most common persistence mechanism after any successful compromise of the management plane.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events for object creation under system.admin.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.admin" action="Add"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj
tuning_guidance: Correlate with change-management tickets; automate a daily diff of the admin roster against an approved-accounts lookup.
investigation_steps: Verify the new account against an approved-accounts list or change ticket.
Check the assigned profile (see FGT-022 for super_admin specifically).
response_guidance: Disable/delete the account immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Granted super_admin Profile
description: An administrator account (new or existing) is assigned the built-in super_admin access profile, the highest privilege level on the device. This is the single riskiest administrator-management event in the catalogue and should be rare and change-ticket-backed.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events on system.admin where the accprofile attribute is set to super_admin.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.admin" cfgattr="accprofile" cfgattr="*super_admin*"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning — every occurrence should have a corresponding change record.
investigation_steps: Verify against change management.
Check what the target account did immediately afterward (FGT-020 sequence).
response_guidance: Downgrade the profile immediately if unauthorized; treat the granting administrator's session as suspect.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Account Deleted
description: An administrator account is deleted. Can be routine offboarding, but an attacker who has planted a persistence account may also delete legitimate accounts to remove competing access or hinder incident response.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events for object deletion under system.admin.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.admin" action="Delete"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj
tuning_guidance: Correlate with HR/offboarding workflows for routine cases.
investigation_steps: Confirm the deleted account against offboarding records.
Check for a corresponding new-account-creation event around the same time (account swap pattern).
response_guidance: Investigate if the deletion is unaccounted for, particularly if it removes a legitimate security-team account.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Password Changed by Another Administrator
description: An administrator's password is changed by a session authenticated as a different user. Could be legitimate password-reset assistance, or an attacker locking the legitimate owner out of their own account after taking it over.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrator password-change events with acting and target user.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events where cfgattr=password and the acting user field differs from the target account (cfgobj).
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.admin" cfgattr="password"
| where user!=cfgobj
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj
tuning_guidance: Expected for designated helpdesk/security-team accounts performing resets — allowlist those actors.
investigation_steps: Contact the affected account owner to confirm they requested the reset.
Check for a subsequent successful login by the resetting administrator using the target's account.
response_guidance: If unconfirmed, treat as account takeover: reset the credential again and lock the account pending investigation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate SD-WAN Configuration Changed
description: SD-WAN rule, member interface, or performance-SLA configuration is modified. Beyond routine tuning, SD-WAN member/route changes can silently redirect traffic that was expected to traverse an inspected path (e.g. through IPS/SSL-inspection-enabled WAN member) onto a less-inspected link.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under the system.sdwan configuration path.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.sdwan"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr, action
tuning_guidance: High-frequency during initial SD-WAN rollout — expect noise; focus on changes outside that window.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether the change routes traffic away from an inspected WAN member.
Cross-reference against a change ticket.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized routing changes and verify inspection coverage on all active WAN members.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Address or Service Object Created or Modified
description: An address object/group or service object/group is created or modified. These are the building blocks firewall policies reference; a subtly-widened address group (e.g. changing a /32 to a /24, or adding 0.0.0.0/0) can silently broaden every policy that references it without the policy itself appearing to change.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under firewall.address*, firewall.addrgrp, firewall.service.custom, and firewall.service.group.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="firewall.address*" OR cfgpath="firewall.addrgrp" OR cfgpath="firewall.service.custom" OR cfgpath="firewall.service.group")
| table _time, devname, user, cfgpath, cfgobj, action
tuning_guidance: High-frequency in dynamic environments; focus alerting on objects referenced by Internet-facing policies (join against a policy-to-object mapping).
investigation_steps: Diff the object's old and new value if available in the log payload.
Check which firewall policies reference this object (FGT-030 for the policy-level view).
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized broadening; audit all policies referencing the object.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VIP or Virtual Server Created
description: A new Virtual IP (VIP/DNAT) or load-balancing virtual server is created, mapping an external address/port to an internal host. This is precisely how an internal service becomes reachable from the Internet — a new VIP pointing at RDP, SSH, SMB, or a database port is a critical finding (see FGT-034/035/036 for the specific inbound-exposure detections).
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events for new firewall.vip objects.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.vip" action="Add"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned service publication; require a change ticket referencing the exposed port for anything beyond HTTPS (443).
investigation_steps: Look up the extport/mappedport the VIP exposes.
Check whether a firewall policy referencing this VIP was also created (FGT-030) and whether it is enabled.
response_guidance: Disable the VIP immediately if it exposes a sensitive port without authorization.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599.001: Network Address Translation Traversal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Route or Policy Route Changed
description: A static route or policy-based route is added, deleted, or modified. Route changes can redirect traffic around inspection points, or (in a more advanced scenario) enable traffic interception/collection by routing sensitive subnets through an attacker-influenced next-hop.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under router.static and router.policy.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="router.static" OR cfgpath="router.policy")
| table _time, devname, user, cfgpath, cfgobj, action
tuning_guidance: Expected during network changes/migrations; alert with higher priority on routes affecting 0.0.0.0/0 or core subnets.
investigation_steps: Confirm the new next-hop is a known, trusted gateway.
Check whether the change correlates with an unusual login (FGT-005/006).
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized routing changes immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VDOM, Interface, or DHCP Configuration Changed
description: A VDOM, physical/VLAN interface, or DHCP server configuration is created or modified — including an interface's administrative access permissions (which protocols/roles, e.g. HTTPS/SSH/ping, are allowed on it). Enabling administrative access on a WAN-facing interface is the single most common way a FortiGate management plane becomes Internet-exposed.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under system.interface, system.vdom, and system.dhcp, with a specific highlight on the allowaccess attribute.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="system.interface" OR cfgpath="system.vdom" OR cfgpath="system.dhcp")
| eval is_admin_access_change=if(cfgattr="allowaccess",1,0)
| table _time, devname, user, cfgpath, cfgobj, cfgattr, is_admin_access_change
tuning_guidance: Prioritize alerting where is_admin_access_change=1 and the interface role is WAN — this is the FGT-006 exposure scenario at its root cause.
investigation_steps: If allowaccess was changed, check which protocols were added and on which interface (WAN vs. internal).
Cross-reference with FGT-006 for any subsequent login on that interface.
response_guidance: Remove administrative access from WAN interfaces immediately unless explicitly required and compensating controls (trusted-hosts, non-standard port, MFA) are in place.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Firewall Policy Created, Modified, or Deleted
description: The baseline detection for any firewall-policy configuration event (creation, edit, or deletion). Serves as the anchor for the more specific, higher-severity policy-weakening detections that follow (FGT-031 through FGT-039), and gives full audit coverage of the object attackers most directly manipulate to open network access.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under firewall.policy for any action.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, action, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: High-frequency in change-managed environments; consider routing this as an audit trail feed rather than a standalone alert, and rely on FGT-031+ for alerting.
investigation_steps: Identify policyid and diff against known-good baseline or FortiManager revision history if available.
response_guidance: No automatic response; feeds downstream detections.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate ANY/ANY Firewall Policy Created
description: A firewall policy is created or modified so that source address, destination address, and service are all set to ALL (or an equivalent 0.0.0.0/0 address object). This is the single most dangerous policy misconfiguration on a FortiGate — it collapses network segmentation entirely for whichever interfaces the policy binds.
detection_logic: Filters policy configuration events where srcaddr, dstaddr, and service are all set to the ALL object.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy"
| search srcaddr="all" dstaddr="all" service="ALL"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, srcintf, dstintf
tuning_guidance: No legitimate ongoing use case in a segmented network — reserve exceptions only for explicitly documented lab/test VDOMs isolated from production.
investigation_steps: Identify the interfaces the policy binds (srcintf/dstintf) — WAN-to-LAN is the most critical case.
Check whether the policy is enabled and what traffic has already matched it.
response_guidance: Disable the policy immediately; this should page the on-call security engineer regardless of time of day.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Firewall Policy Source or Destination Broadened to ALL
description: An existing firewall policy's source or destination address is changed to the ALL object while the other side and service remain scoped — a partial version of FGT-031, still a significant segmentation weakening (e.g. a policy that previously restricted source to a management subnet now accepts traffic from anywhere).
detection_logic: Filters policy edits where cfgattr is srcaddr or dstaddr and the new value includes the ALL object.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" (cfgattr="srcaddr" OR cfgattr="dstaddr")
| search cfgattr_value="all" OR cfgattr_value="ALL"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr, cfgattr_value
tuning_guidance: Some environments legitimately use ALL for destination on outbound web-browsing policies with security profiles attached — cross-check whether security profiles remain applied (FGT-034/035/036) before treating as high severity.
investigation_steps: Determine which side (src/dst) broadened and the policy's direction.
Check whether security profiles are still attached (reduces but does not eliminate risk).
response_guidance: Revert unless explicitly justified and compensated for with security profiles.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Firewall Policy Action Changed From Deny to Accept
description: A policy's action attribute is changed from deny/block to accept. This flips a policy from an explicit block rule (often used to document and enforce a segmentation boundary) into a permit rule — one of the more subtle ways to quietly open access without touching address or service objects.
detection_logic: Filters policy edits where cfgattr=action and the new value is accept, joined against the policy's prior known state where available.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" cfgattr="action"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Requires the config-change log to include before/after values (version-dependent) to reliably identify deny->accept vs. accept->deny; without it, treat every action-attribute change on a previously-deny policy as worth reviewing.
investigation_steps: Confirm the previous action value via FortiManager revision history or a recent config backup diff.
Identify what traffic is now permitted that was previously blocked.
response_guidance: Revert unless authorized; audit for a corresponding new inbound connection.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Firewall Policy Security Profiles Removed
description: One or more security profiles (IPS, Antivirus, Application Control, Web Filter, DLP, SSL inspection) are removed from a firewall policy, or logging is disabled on it. This is the network-policy equivalent of disabling auditd on a Linux host — the policy keeps passing traffic, but detection and prevention capability on that traffic is gone.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Policy security-profile and logtraffic attribute changes.

detection_logic: Filters policy edits where cfgattr matches a security-profile field (ips-sensor, av-profile, application-list, webfilter-profile, dlp-sensor, ssl-ssh-profile) or logtraffic being disabled.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy"
(cfgattr="ips-sensor" OR cfgattr="av-profile" OR cfgattr="application-list" OR cfgattr="webfilter-profile" OR cfgattr="dlp-sensor" OR cfgattr="ssl-ssh-profile" OR cfgattr="logtraffic")
| eval removed=if(match(_raw,"(?i)(disable|none|\"\")"),1,0)
| where removed=1
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Some internal-only, already-segmented policies legitimately run without deep inspection for performance reasons — maintain an explicit exception list rather than suppressing broadly.
investigation_steps: Identify which profile(s) were removed and the policy's exposure (Internet-facing weighs heaviest).
Check for a subsequent malware/IPS event on traffic that would have matched this policy.
response_guidance: Re-attach security profiles immediately for any Internet-facing or high-risk policy; treat as Critical when combined with an unusual admin login (FGT-020 sequence).

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Firewall Policy Schedule Broadened or Policy Enabled Unexpectedly
description: A policy's schedule object is broadened (e.g. from a business-hours window to 'always'), or a previously-disabled policy is re-enabled. Attackers sometimes prefer enabling a dormant, previously-approved-looking policy rather than creating a new one that would stand out in an audit.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Policy schedule and enable/disable status changes.

detection_logic: Filters policy edits where cfgattr is schedule or status, focused on transitions to 'always' or 'enable'.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" (cfgattr="schedule" OR cfgattr="status")
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference re-enabled policies against a list of intentionally-disabled/deprecated policies maintained by the network team.
investigation_steps: Determine why the policy was originally disabled/scheduled.
Check what traffic has matched it since being enabled/broadened.
response_guidance: Disable/revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New FortiGate Inbound Internet-Facing Firewall Policy
description: A new firewall policy is created with srcintf bound to the WAN/Internet-facing interface and dstintf bound to an internal interface — a new inbound path from the Internet into the network. Every such policy should map to a documented, intentional service exposure.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: New policy creation with interface bindings.

detection_logic: Filters new policy creation events where srcintf is a lookup-tagged WAN interface and dstintf is internal.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" action="Add"
| lookup fgt_interface_roles.csv srcintf OUTPUT role as src_role
| lookup fgt_interface_roles.csv dstintf OUTPUT role as dst_role
| where src_role="wan" AND dst_role="lan"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, srcintf, dstintf
tuning_guidance: Maintain fgt_interface_roles.csv per device since interface naming/roles vary by model and deployment.
investigation_steps: Identify the destination service/port and cross-reference against FGT-037/038/039 for specifically dangerous exposed ports.
response_guidance: Confirm against a change ticket; disable if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599.001: Network Address Translation Traversal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Policy Exposes RDP, SSH, SMB, or Database Port to the Internet
description: An inbound Internet-facing policy (or its referenced VIP) exposes a high-risk administrative or database port — RDP (3389), SSH (22), SMB (445), MSSQL (1433), MySQL (3306), PostgreSQL (5432), or Oracle (1521) — directly to the Internet without restriction. These ports are the most consistently exploited exposure across ransomware and opportunistic-access campaigns.
detection_logic: Filters new/modified inbound policies and VIPs where the referenced service or mapped port matches a high-risk port list.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="firewall.policy" OR cfgpath="firewall.vip")
| lookup fgt_highrisk_ports.csv service OUTPUT is_highrisk
| where is_highrisk="true" OR mappedport IN ("3389","22","445","1433","3306","5432","1521")
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, service, mappedport
tuning_guidance: Zero acceptable steady-state occurrences in most environments; any legitimate exception (e.g. a bastion SSH host) should be documented with source-IP restriction, not open to any/any.
investigation_steps: Confirm the policy restricts source address — an exposed high-risk port with srcaddr=all is an emergency.
Check for inbound connection attempts against the exposed port immediately after the change.
response_guidance: Disable the exposure immediately; this should be a page-worthy, same-hour response regardless of change-ticket status pending verification.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New FortiGate Outbound Unrestricted Firewall Policy
description: A new outbound (LAN-to-WAN) policy is created with broad destination/service scope and no security profiles attached. Unrestricted outbound access is a common enabler for both C2 callback and data exfiltration once an internal host is compromised.
detection_logic: Filters new policy creation where srcintf is internal, dstintf is WAN, dstaddr is ALL, and no security profiles are attached.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" action="Add"
| lookup fgt_interface_roles.csv srcintf OUTPUT role as src_role
| lookup fgt_interface_roles.csv dstintf OUTPUT role as dst_role
| where src_role="lan" AND dst_role="wan" AND dstaddr="all"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, service
tuning_guidance: Common for general web-browsing policies — the alert-worthy variant is specifically the combination of unrestricted scope AND missing security profiles (cross-reference FGT-034).
investigation_steps: Confirm whether IPS/AV/web-filter profiles are attached despite broad scope.
Review outbound traffic volume from hosts matching this policy after creation.
response_guidance: Attach appropriate security profiles or scope the policy down.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Login Followed by Policy Modification and New Inbound Connection
description: The firewall-compromise sequence prioritized by the master specification: an administrative login, followed by a firewall policy modification that broadens access, followed by a new inbound connection matching the modified policy — all within one correlation window. This is the clearest end-to-end signature of a compromised administrator being used to open network access for follow-on activity.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event + traffic log
data_sources.description: Login, policy-change, and subsequent traffic events correlated by policy id and time.

detection_logic: Correlates an admin login, a firewall.policy change event referencing a policyid, and a traffic-log accept event matching that same policyid, all within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system action="login" status="success"
| eval stage="1_login"
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" | eval stage="2_policy_change", policyid=cfgobj ]
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward action="accept" | eval stage="3_new_traffic" ]
| transaction devname maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, policyid, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires joining across event and traffic sourcetypes and normalizing policyid presence in both — validate field extraction on both sourcetypes before enabling as a production alert.
investigation_steps: Identify the exact policy change and the traffic that subsequently matched it.
Treat as a live incident pending confirmation of legitimacy.
response_guidance: Disable the policy and suspend the administrator account pending investigation; this sequence should trigger immediate incident response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: login -> policy change -> matching traffic accept

title: FortiGate Logging or Log Destination Disabled
description: Global traffic/event/security logging is disabled, or a syslog/FortiAnalyzer log destination is removed or redirected. Whether by disabling logging outright or by silently changing where logs go, this is the FortiGate equivalent of stopping auditd — a near-universal precursor step before other unauthorized changes so they leave no trail.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Logging configuration changes: global toggles and destination settings.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under any log.* path where status is set to disable or a server-address attribute changes.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="log.*"
| where cfgattr="status" OR cfgattr="server" OR cfgattr="*fortianalyzer*"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgpath, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate use case for disabling logging outright; log-destination migrations should be rare, planned, and change-ticket-backed.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether this was a planned FortiAnalyzer/syslog migration.
Check what other configuration changes occurred immediately before or after (this is frequently step one of FGT-020/FGT-041).
response_guidance: Re-enable logging immediately; treat the acting session as compromised until proven otherwise and audit everything that happened while logging was off using local disk logs or the FortiGate's own memory buffer if still available.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Security Profile Globally Disabled (IPS / AV / Web Filter / DNS Filter / App Control / DLP / SSL Inspection)
description: A UTM security profile is deleted or disabled at the profile level (as opposed to being unlinked from one policy, see FGT-034) — meaning every policy referencing it silently loses that inspection capability at once. This is broader-blast-radius than a single-policy change and should be treated with correspondingly higher urgency.
detection_logic: Filters delete events under any UTM profile configuration path.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system
(cfgpath="ips.sensor" OR cfgpath="antivirus.profile" OR cfgpath="webfilter.profile" OR cfgpath="application.list" OR cfgpath="dlp.sensor" OR cfgpath="firewall.ssl-ssh-profile")
action="Delete"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgpath, cfgobj
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during profile consolidation/refactoring; require the replacement profile to be applied to affected policies in the same maintenance window.
investigation_steps: Identify every policy that referenced the deleted profile.
Check for a replacement profile applied at the same time — its absence means those policies are now uninspected.
response_guidance: Restore or replace the profile immediately across all affected policies.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Administrator Login Followed by Logging Disabled and Security Profile Removed
description: The defense-evasion sequence prioritized by the master specification: an admin login followed by logging being weakened and a security profile or IPS/AV control being disabled, all within one session window. Treated as Critical regardless of the individual severities of its components, because the combination specifically targets the organization's ability to detect what happens next.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Login and logging/security-profile-weakening events correlated by user/session.

detection_logic: Correlates a successful admin login with a subsequent logging-configuration change and a subsequent security-profile disable/removal, for the same user within 20 minutes.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system
| eval stage=case(action="login" AND status="success","1_login", cfgpath="log.*" AND (cfgattr="status" OR cfgattr="server"),"2_logging_weakened", (cfgpath="ips.sensor" OR cfgpath="antivirus.profile" OR cfgpath="firewall.policy") AND (cfgattr="ips-sensor" OR cfgattr="av-profile" OR action="Delete"),"3_control_removed", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=20m startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires the same field-mapping validation as FGT-020; tune the keyword set to your FortiOS version's actual cfgpath/cfgattr naming before enabling as a paging alert.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Restore logging and security controls immediately.
Review all traffic that occurred while controls were down.
response_guidance: Isolate the device from remote management, restore configuration from known-good backup, initiate incident response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: login -> logging weakened -> security control removed

title: FortiGate Configuration Backup Exported
description: The full running configuration is exported (backup) via GUI, CLI, or API. A configuration export can contain encrypted secrets, PSKs, and certificate references — treat repeated or unusual-actor exports as potential configuration/credential collection rather than routine change-management hygiene.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for configuration backup/export actions.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*config*backup*" OR msg="*configuration file*")
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, msg
tuning_guidance: Baseline expected automated nightly backups (a known service account/scheduler) separately from interactive exports.
investigation_steps: Confirm the exporting account matches the expected backup automation or a routine change-ticket-backed export.
response_guidance: No action for expected exports; escalate per FGT-044 for repeated/unusual-actor exports.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1005: Data from Local System

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated FortiGate Configuration Exports by an Unusual Administrator
description: Multiple configuration exports within a short window, or an export by an administrator account not associated with the expected backup automation. Consistent with an attacker collecting full device configuration (including references to secrets) for offline analysis or exfiltration.
detection_logic: Counts configuration exports per user in a rolling window and flags accounts not on the known-automation allowlist.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*config*backup*" OR msg="*configuration file*")
| lookup fgt_backup_automation_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_automation
| where isnull(is_automation)
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count by user, srcip, _time
| where count>=2
tuning_guidance: Maintain the automation-account allowlist; adjust threshold for organizations with frequent legitimate manual exports.
investigation_steps: Confirm the exporting account and its business justification.
Check whether the exported configuration was subsequently transferred off the management network (correlate with any large HTTPS/SCP upload, FGT-090+ exfiltration detections).
response_guidance: Investigate as potential configuration/credential collection; rotate any secrets referenced in the configuration if compromise is suspected.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1005: Data from Local System

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Configuration Restore or Rollback
description: A configuration file is uploaded/restored, or the device is rolled back to a prior configuration revision. Can silently undo recent security hardening or, conversely, be used by an attacker to push a modified configuration wholesale rather than making incremental changes that are individually more visible.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for configuration restore/upload/rollback actions.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*config*restore*" OR msg="*rollback*")
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, msg
tuning_guidance: Should always correlate with a planned maintenance window; treat any restore outside one as high priority.
investigation_steps: Diff the restored configuration against the immediately-prior running configuration to identify exactly what changed.
Verify the source of the uploaded configuration file.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, restore from a known-good backup and audit the full configuration for tampering.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601.002: Downgrade System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Factory Reset
description: The device is reset to factory defaults, wiping the entire configuration including logging destinations, firewall policies, and administrator accounts. In a production device this is either a catastrophic mistake or a deliberate act of sabotage/anti-forensics — either way it removes the very audit trail needed to investigate it.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Factory reset event, if captured before the device wipes local logging state.

detection_logic: Filters system event log for factory-reset action; also relies on FortiAnalyzer/syslog receiving the event externally since local logs are destroyed by the reset itself.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system msg="*factory*reset*"
| table _time, devname, user, srcip
tuning_guidance: No tuning — this should never occur on a production device outside a fully-documented decommissioning process.
investigation_steps: Confirm against decommissioning records.
If unexpected, treat as a security incident and preserve any external (FortiAnalyzer/syslog) logs immediately before they age out.
response_guidance: Isolate the device, restore from backup, and treat this as a confirmed incident requiring full investigation of how reset-level access was obtained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Firmware Upgrade or Downgrade
description: Firmware is changed. An upgrade is routine maintenance; a downgrade is far more suspicious — it can reintroduce previously-patched vulnerabilities or strip newer security-hardening defaults, and is a documented technique in real Fortinet-targeting campaigns to re-expose a known exploit path.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Firmware change events with old/new version.

detection_logic: Filters system event log for firmware-change events and flags version-downgrade cases specifically.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system msg="*firmware*"
| rex field=msg "from (?<old_version>[\d\.]+) to (?<new_version>[\d\.]+)"
| eval is_downgrade=if(old_version>new_version,1,0)
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, old_version, new_version, is_downgrade
tuning_guidance: Version comparison via simple string ordering is unreliable across FortiOS's version scheme — use a proper semver comparison in production; the SPL above is illustrative.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket for planned upgrades.
For downgrades, verify the source of the firmware image and whether it was digitally signed/validated by the device.
response_guidance: Treat unauthorized downgrades as Critical defense evasion; re-upgrade and audit configuration for tampering introduced during the downgraded window.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601.002: Downgrade System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Unexpected Reboot, Shutdown, or Mass Reboot
description: The device reboots or shuts down outside a scheduled maintenance window, or (fleet-wide, see FNT-X-###) many FortiGates reboot within a short window of each other. Isolated reboots are often benign (firmware apply, HA event); mass, unscheduled reboots are consistent with a fleet-wide disruptive action via FortiManager or direct compromise.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for reboot/shutdown events outside a maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*reboot*" OR msg="*shutdown*")
| lookup fgt_maintenance_windows.csv devname _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window)
| table _time, devname, user, msg
tuning_guidance: Maintain a maintenance-window lookup keyed by device and time range; without it, expect noise from routine patching cycles.
investigation_steps: Identify the triggering user/process (manual vs. HA failover vs. crash).
Check whether other FortiGates rebooted in the same window (fleet-wide correlation).
response_guidance: Investigate crash logs for unexpected reboots; escalate immediately if correlated across multiple devices without a corresponding FortiManager-initiated maintenance job.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate HA Configuration Changed or HA Member Added/Removed
description: High-availability cluster membership or configuration is changed — a new HA member added, an existing one removed, or failover/priority settings modified. An attacker who can add a rogue HA member effectively gains the ability to synchronize their own device's configuration into the cluster.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under system.ha.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="system.ha"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgattr, action
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned HA rollout/maintenance; require a change ticket for membership changes outside that window.
investigation_steps: Verify the identity and integrity of any newly-added HA member.
Check for a subsequent unexpected failover event.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized HA members immediately; verify configuration sync did not propagate malicious changes.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Hostname, System Time, or NTP/DNS Server Changed
description: The device hostname, system clock, or NTP/DNS server configuration is changed. Time manipulation is a classic anti-forensics technique that skews log timestamps relative to other sources, complicating timeline reconstruction across the Security Fabric; DNS server changes can also be used to redirect the device's own resolution (including FortiGuard update checks) through an attacker-controlled resolver.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under system.ntp, system.dns, and the hostname attribute of system.global.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="system.ntp" OR cfgpath="system.dns" OR (cfgpath="system.global" AND cfgattr="hostname"))
| table _time, devname, user, cfgpath, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during initial provisioning or infrastructure migration — treat post-deployment changes as higher priority.
investigation_steps: Verify new NTP/DNS servers are known-good infrastructure.
Check for a discontinuity in the device's log timestamps around the change.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes; if time was manipulated, reconcile the affected log window against FortiAnalyzer's own receipt timestamps.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Login Failure
description: A single failed SSL VPN or IPsec remote-access authentication attempt. The atomic building block for the VPN brute-force/spray/successful-after-failures detections below — VPN portals are one of the most consistently targeted Internet-facing Fortinet surfaces.
detection_logic: Filters VPN subtype events for failed authentication.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="ssl-login-fail"
| table _time, devname, user, srcip, reason
tuning_guidance: Not alert-worthy alone; use FGT-052/053 for volume-based detection.
investigation_steps: Confirm the source IP against known remote-user ranges.
response_guidance: No action for isolated failures.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Brute Force
description: Repeated SSL VPN/IPsec authentication failures for a single account within a short window — sustained password guessing against a specific known or guessed VPN username.
detection_logic: Counts VPN login failures per user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="ssl-login-fail"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, values(srcip) as source_ips, dc(srcip) as distinct_sources by user, _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Raise threshold for accounts behind CGNAT ranges where legitimate retries from many exit IPs may occur.
investigation_steps: Check whether the targeted account is valid.
Check for a subsequent success (FGT-054).
response_guidance: Lock the targeted account temporarily; block the source IP(s) at the perimeter.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Password Spraying
description: A single source IP attempting VPN authentication against many distinct usernames — the VPN-portal equivalent of FGT-003, and one of the most common real-world attack patterns against Fortinet SSL VPN given how frequently VPN username enumeration/breach-list credentials are used at scale.

data_sources.name: FortiGate VPN log
data_sources.description: VPN authentication failures with source IP and username.

detection_logic: Counts distinct usernames attempted per source IP in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="ssl-login-fail"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(user) as distinct_users, values(user) as usernames_tried, count by srcip, _time
| where distinct_users>=6
tuning_guidance: Exclude known scanning/research ranges if separately tracked; otherwise this pattern is high-signal against VPN portals specifically.
investigation_steps: Check whether any of usernames_tried are valid.
Check for any success from the same source (FGT-054).
response_guidance: Block the source IP; enforce/verify MFA for all VPN accounts; consider geo-fencing the VPN portal if the source is a known-bad region.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful FortiGate VPN Login Following Repeated Failures
description: A successful VPN login for a user/source pair that had five or more failures in the preceding 30 minutes — the VPN equivalent of FGT-004, and given how many real intrusions in 2023-2024 began with exactly this pattern against FortiGate SSL VPN, one of the highest-priority detections in the entire library.
detection_logic: Joins a failed-VPN-login threshold search with a subsequent VPN login success for the same user within the correlation window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn (action="ssl-login-fail" OR action="ssl-login")
| eval outcome=if(action="ssl-login-fail","fail","success")
| transaction user maxspan=30m startswith=eval(outcome="fail") endswith=eval(outcome="success")
| where eventcount>=6
| table _time, user, srcip, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference srcip against a known-user-location baseline before treating as fully confirmed compromise, but default to high-confidence given how targeted this pattern is in the wild.
investigation_steps: Force-terminate the VPN session immediately pending verification.
Review all internal connections made from the VPN-assigned IP for this session (see FGT-060+ lateral-movement detections).
Check the account's MFA enrollment status.
response_guidance: Disconnect the session, disable the account, and force credential/MFA reset; treat as a confirmed intrusion until proven otherwise and begin internal-network hunting from the VPN-assigned address.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Source IP or Geographic Anomaly for FortiGate VPN User
description: A successful VPN login from a source IP/geography never seen for that user, or two concurrent VPN sessions for the same user from geographically distant locations in a timeframe that would be physically impossible to travel between ("impossible travel") where geo-IP enrichment is available.

data_sources.name: FortiGate VPN log
data_sources.description: VPN login success events with source IP.

detection_logic: Builds a per-user baseline of source IPs/countries over 30 days and flags first-seen values; separately flags overlapping sessions with implausible travel time between enriched geolocations.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="ssl-login"
| iplocation srcip
| eval country=Country
[ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="ssl-login" earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h
  | iplocation srcip | stats count by user, Country | rename Country as known_country | fields user, known_country | format ]
| where NOT country=known_country
| table _time, user, srcip, country
tuning_guidance: Best implemented as a maintained per-user country/ASN baseline lookup rather than the illustrative subsearch shown; mobile users on VPN providers will need an explicit exception path.
investigation_steps: Confirm travel/location change with the user directly.
Check for concurrent sessions from two different locations (true impossible-travel case).
response_guidance: If unconfirmed, disconnect the session and treat as potential account compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Login Outside Normal Hours or Excessive Reconnects
description: A VPN session begins well outside the user's normal working hours, or the same account reconnects an unusually high number of times in a short period (consistent with an unstable C2 tunnel or automated reconnection tooling rather than a human user).
detection_logic: Flags off-hours logins per a configured business-hours window, and counts tunnel-up events per user in a rolling window for the reconnect-volume case.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="tunnel-up"
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as reconnects, values(hour) as hours by user, _time
| where reconnects>=10 OR (hours<"06" OR hours>="22")
tuning_guidance: Tune business hours per region/user group; exclude known always-on site-to-site tunnels which reconnect frequently by design (filter on tunnel type where available).
investigation_steps: Confirm whether off-hours access is expected (on-call) or unusual for this user.
For excessive reconnects, check whether this is a flaky client/network vs. automated tooling.
response_guidance: Use as a contributing signal for correlation rather than standalone action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Dormant or Privileged FortiGate VPN Account Used
description: A VPN login succeeds for an account that has not authenticated in 90+ days (dormant), or for an account known to hold privileged internal access (domain admin, backup operator, etc.). Dormant-account use is a classic sign of a stale credential being exploited; privileged-account VPN use deserves elevated scrutiny regardless of pattern.

data_sources.name: FortiGate VPN log
data_sources.description: VPN login success events cross-referenced against last-seen and privilege lookups.

detection_logic: Joins VPN login success against a last-authenticated-date lookup (dormancy) and a privileged-account lookup.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="ssl-login"
| lookup fgt_vpn_last_seen.csv user OUTPUT last_seen
| lookup fgt_privileged_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_privileged
| eval days_dormant=round((now()-strptime(last_seen,"%Y-%m-%d"))/86400,0)
| where days_dormant>=90 OR is_privileged="true"
| table _time, user, srcip, days_dormant, is_privileged
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained last-seen lookup, ideally refreshed nightly; without it this degrades to the privileged-account case only.
investigation_steps: Confirm the account owner initiated this session.
For dormant accounts, verify whether the account should have been disabled as part of offboarding.
response_guidance: Disable dormant accounts that should not still be active; require re-verification (help desk callback) before allowing continued privileged VPN access.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Session Followed by Internal Reconnaissance
description: A VPN client IP is observed generating a broad sweep of internal connection attempts (many distinct internal destinations and/or ports) shortly after establishing a tunnel — consistent with an attacker who has just gained VPN access performing network discovery before further lateral movement.

data_sources.name: FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: Internal traffic originating from the VPN-assigned address pool.

detection_logic: Filters forward traffic where srcip falls in the VPN address pool and counts distinct internal destination IP/port pairs in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward
| lookup fgt_vpn_pools.csv srcip OUTPUT is_vpn_pool
| where is_vpn_pool="true"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats dc(dstip) as distinct_dests, dc(dstport) as distinct_ports, values(dstport) as ports by srcip, user, _time
| where distinct_dests>=20 OR distinct_ports>=15
tuning_guidance: Exclude known vulnerability-scanner or asset-inventory service accounts that legitimately sweep the internal network from a VPN-adjacent jump host.
investigation_steps: Identify the connecting user account and correlate with FGT-054/055.
Review which internal hosts/ports were scanned for signs of a targeted follow-up (RDP/SMB/SSH concentration, see FGT-060).
response_guidance: Disconnect the VPN session and investigate as an active intrusion.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1046: Network Service Discovery
MITRE ATT&CK T1018: Remote System Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Session Followed by RDP, SMB, or SSH to Multiple Internal Hosts
description: A single VPN-assigned source IP initiates RDP, SMB, or SSH connections to multiple distinct internal hosts shortly after tunnel establishment — the traffic-level signature of lateral movement following VPN-based initial access, and the direct continuation of the FGT-058 reconnaissance pattern into actual targeted connections.

data_sources.name: FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: Internal RDP/SMB/SSH traffic originating from the VPN pool.

detection_logic: Filters forward traffic from the VPN address pool for RDP/SMB/SSH services and counts distinct internal destinations per source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward (service="RDP" OR service="SMB" OR dstport=22)
| lookup fgt_vpn_pools.csv srcip OUTPUT is_vpn_pool
| where is_vpn_pool="true" AND action="accept"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(dstip) as distinct_dests, values(dstip) as destinations by srcip, user, service, _time
| where distinct_dests>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known jump-host/bastion accounts whose entire purpose is administering many internal hosts via RDP/SSH — maintain that allowlist explicitly.
investigation_steps: Treat as an active lateral-movement incident pending verification.
Identify the account and every destination host touched.
Check destination hosts for subsequent signs of compromise (new accounts, malware).
response_guidance: Disconnect the VPN session immediately; isolate touched internal hosts pending investigation; this should trigger incident response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol
MITRE ATT&CK T1021.002: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Session Followed by LDAP/Kerberos Activity Against Domain Controller
