description: A VPN client connects to LDAP (389/636) or Kerberos (88) ports on a domain controller shortly after tunnel establishment — consistent with directory enumeration or credential-attack tooling (e.g. Kerberoasting, AD reconnaissance frameworks) being run from a freshly-obtained VPN foothold.

data_sources.name: FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: Internal LDAP/Kerberos traffic originating from the VPN pool toward known domain controllers.

detection_logic: Filters forward traffic from the VPN pool to LDAP/Kerberos ports on hosts tagged as domain controllers.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward (dstport=389 OR dstport=636 OR dstport=88)
| lookup fgt_vpn_pools.csv srcip OUTPUT is_vpn_pool
| lookup fgt_domain_controllers.csv dstip OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_vpn_pool="true" AND is_dc="true" AND action="accept"
| table _time, srcip, user, dstip, dstport
tuning_guidance: Exclude known identity-management/helpdesk service accounts with a legitimate business reason to query AD directly over VPN.
investigation_steps: Correlate with domain-controller-side authentication/LDAP query logs if available (outside this catalogue's scope) for the specific queries made.
Check for subsequent ticket-request anomalies.
response_guidance: Disconnect and investigate; treat as a credential-access attempt pending confirmation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1558: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate SSL VPN Newly Enabled
description: SSL VPN service is enabled on the device (or on an interface) where it was previously disabled. This is the direct precursor to standing up a new Internet-facing remote-access path, and worth alerting on independent of whether the VPN is subsequently abused.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under vpn.ssl.settings where the service is enabled or a listen interface is added.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="vpn.ssl.settings"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgattr, action
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned VPN rollout; require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm against change management.
Verify MFA is enforced on the newly-enabled portal before it goes live.
response_guidance: Disable immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1133: External Remote Services

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Multi-Factor Authentication Removed
description: MFA/FortiToken enforcement is removed from an SSL VPN portal or user group. Given how consistently credential-based VPN compromise appears in real incidents (FGT-054), removing MFA from the VPN is one of the highest-impact single changes an attacker (or a well-meaning but risky administrator) can make.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events where a VPN-associated user group's two-factor requirement is disabled.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="user.group" cfgattr="*two-factor*"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate case for removing MFA from a VPN group outside an emergency-access procedure.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification immediately.
Check for subsequent VPN logins by members of the affected group.
response_guidance: Re-enable MFA immediately unless explicitly authorized and time-boxed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Full-Tunnel VPN Changed to Split Tunnel
description: An SSL VPN portal's tunnel mode is changed from full-tunnel (all client traffic routed through and inspected by the FortiGate) to split-tunnel (only corporate-destined traffic is routed through the tunnel). This removes visibility and inspection of the remote user's general Internet traffic, expanding the client's effective attack surface while connected.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events on split-tunneling attribute transitioning to enabled.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="vpn.ssl.web.portal" cfgattr="split-tunneling"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for bandwidth/performance reasons in some environments — require a documented security exception given the visibility tradeoff.
investigation_steps: Confirm the change is intentional and approved.
Assess whether endpoint protection compensates for the reduced network-level visibility.
response_guidance: Revert to full-tunnel for high-risk user groups if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate IPsec PSK or Tunnel Configuration Changed
description: A site-to-site IPsec tunnel's pre-shared key, phase 1/2 proposal, or peer configuration is changed, or a new tunnel is created. A modified peer address or weakened encryption proposal on an existing tunnel can redirect or expose site-to-site traffic; a new tunnel is a new trust relationship that deserves the same scrutiny as a new VIP.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under vpn.ipsec.phase1-interface and phase2-interface, highlighting psksecret and proposal attribute changes.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="vpn.ipsec.phase1-interface" OR cfgpath="vpn.ipsec.phase2-interface")
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr, action
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned site-to-site changes; require validation that the encryption proposal was not weakened (see FGT-065).
investigation_steps: Confirm the peer address/PSK change against a change ticket.
Verify no proposal downgrade occurred.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized tunnel changes and rotate the PSK.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate VPN Weak Encryption or Legacy Protocol/Cipher Introduced
description: An IPsec phase 1/2 proposal or SSL VPN cipher configuration is changed to a legacy/weak algorithm (e.g. DES/3DES, MD5, SHA1-only, or a deprecated SSL/TLS version). This can be a subtle downgrade attack enabler or, more commonly, evidence of a misconfigured or aging tunnel that never got hardened.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events where the new proposal/cipher value matches a maintained weak-algorithm list.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgattr="proposal" OR cfgattr="ssl-min-proto-ver")
| lookup fgt_weak_crypto.csv cfgattr_value OUTPUT is_weak
| where is_weak="true"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr, cfgattr_value
tuning_guidance: Maintain fgt_weak_crypto.csv against current organizational cryptographic standards; review periodically as guidance evolves.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether this is a legacy compatibility requirement (e.g. an old peer device) with a documented risk acceptance.
response_guidance: Harden to current recommended proposals unless a documented, time-boxed exception exists.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Port Scan Detected (Vertical)
description: A single source IP contacts many distinct destination ports on a single destination host in a short window — a vertical port scan, typically used to fingerprint which services a specific host exposes.
detection_logic: Counts distinct destination ports per (srcip, dstip) pair in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward
| bin _time span=5m
| stats dc(dstport) as distinct_ports by srcip, dstip, _time
| where distinct_ports>=20
tuning_guidance: Exclude known internal vulnerability-scanner service accounts/subnets.
investigation_steps: Determine whether srcip is internal (compromised host doing recon) or external.
Check whether any of the scanned ports subsequently received a full connection.
response_guidance: Block the source if external and unexpected; investigate the source host if internal.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1595.001: Scanning IP Blocks

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Port Scan Detected (Horizontal / Network Sweep)
description: A single source IP contacts the same destination port across many distinct destination hosts in a short window — a horizontal scan/network sweep, typically used to find every host on a network running a specific service (e.g. sweeping for open RDP or SMB across an entire subnet).
detection_logic: Counts distinct destination IPs per (srcip, dstport) pair in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward
| bin _time span=5m
| stats dc(dstip) as distinct_dests by srcip, dstport, _time
| where distinct_dests>=25
tuning_guidance: Exclude known asset-discovery/vulnerability-management scanners.
investigation_steps: Identify the source host and whether it should be performing network-wide scanning.
Check the specific dstport swept for known-dangerous services (RDP/SMB/SSH).
response_guidance: Isolate the source host if internal and unauthorized; block if external.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1595.001: Scanning IP Blocks
MITRE ATT&CK T1018: Remote System Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Distributed Scanning Against a Single Destination
description: Many distinct source IPs scan the same destination host/port combination in a short window — consistent with distributed/botnet-driven vulnerability scanning against an Internet-facing asset, common ahead of mass-exploitation campaigns targeting a newly-disclosed vulnerability.
detection_logic: Counts distinct source IPs per (dstip, dstport) pair in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward action="accept"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats dc(srcip) as distinct_sources by dstip, dstport, _time
| where distinct_sources>=30
tuning_guidance: Expected background noise for well-known ports (443, 80) on Internet-facing hosts — focus this on administrative/less-common ports.
investigation_steps: Identify what service runs on the targeted dstport.
Cross-reference against recently-disclosed vulnerabilities for that service.
response_guidance: Verify patch status of the targeted service; consider geo-fencing or rate-limiting if the pattern continues.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate High Connection Failure Rate From a Single Source
description: A source IP generates an unusually high ratio of denied/failed/timeout connections relative to accepted ones — consistent with automated scanning or probing tools that attempt many connections expecting most to fail.
detection_logic: Computes the ratio of deny/timeout to accept actions per source IP in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count(eval(action="deny" OR action="timeout")) as failed, count(eval(action="accept")) as accepted by srcip, _time
| eval failure_ratio=round(failed/(accepted+1),2)
| where failed>=50 AND failure_ratio>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known internal monitoring/health-check systems that legitimately probe many closed ports.
investigation_steps: Determine if srcip is internal (potential malware performing discovery) or external (scanner).
response_guidance: Investigate source host if internal; no action typically required for external Internet background scanning beyond standard perimeter posture.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1046: Network Service Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate New External Destination Country or ASN for a Host
description: An internal host connects outbound to a country or Autonomous System Number it has never contacted in the prior 30 days. A broad, low-confidence signal on its own, but useful as an enrichment input to the higher-confidence beaconing and C2 detections below.

data_sources.name: FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: Outbound traffic enriched with destination geolocation/ASN.

detection_logic: Builds a 30-day baseline of destination countries/ASNs per internal host and flags first-seen values.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward action="accept" direction="outbound"
| iplocation dstip
| eval dest_country=Country
[ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound" earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h
  | iplocation dstip | stats count by srcip, Country | rename Country as known_country | fields srcip, known_country | format ]
| where NOT dest_country=known_country
| table _time, srcip, dstip, dest_country
tuning_guidance: Best implemented as a maintained per-host baseline lookup, not the illustrative subsearch shown, which will not scale to a production traffic volume.
investigation_steps: Correlate with IPS/AV/web-filter verdicts for the same destination.
Check whether the destination is a known cloud/CDN range (lower risk) vs. an unfamiliar hosting provider.
response_guidance: No automatic action; feeds the C2/beaconing correlation detections.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Unusual Outbound Data Volume From a Single Host
description: An internal host sends a volume of outbound data (sentbyte) significantly above its own historical baseline in a rolling window — a broad exfiltration-adjacent signal that feeds the more specific data-exfiltration detections later in this catalogue.
detection_logic: Aggregates sentbyte per source host per hour and flags values statistically far above that host's 30-day median.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats sum(sentbyte) as total_sent by srcip, _time
| eventstats avg(total_sent) as avg_sent, stdev(total_sent) as stdev_sent by srcip
| eval zscore=round((total_sent-avg_sent)/(stdev_sent+1),2)
| where zscore>=3 AND total_sent>=500000000
tuning_guidance: Exclude known backup/replication/large-file-transfer service accounts and scheduled jobs.
investigation_steps: Identify the destination and correlate with FGT-070 for a first-seen destination.
Check for archive-creation activity on the source host if endpoint telemetry is available.
response_guidance: Investigate the source host and destination; block if destination is confirmed malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: z-score >= 3 over 30-day per-host baseline, minimum 500MB/hour

title: FortiGate Periodic Outbound Beaconing Detected
description: An internal host makes outbound connections to the same destination at unusually regular time intervals — the classic network signature of C2 beaconing, where malware checks in with its controller on a fixed or jittered schedule.
detection_logic: Computes the standard deviation of inter-connection intervals for each (srcip, dstip) pair over a rolling window; low variance combined with a sufficient connection count indicates regular, machine-driven timing.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound" action="accept"
| sort srcip, dstip, _time
| streamstats current=f last(_time) as prev_time by srcip, dstip
| eval interval=_time-prev_time
| where isnotnull(interval)
| stats count as connections, avg(interval) as avg_interval, stdev(interval) as stdev_interval by srcip, dstip
| eval coefficient_of_variation=round(stdev_interval/avg_interval,3)
| where connections>=10 AND coefficient_of_variation<=0.15
tuning_guidance: Exclude known legitimate polling services (monitoring agents, NTP-like check-ins, SaaS heartbeats) via an allowlist of expected regular-interval destinations.
investigation_steps: Identify the destination domain/IP and check reputation/first-seen status (FGT-070).
Check for a corresponding process on the source host if endpoint telemetry (FortiEDR/FortiClient) is available.
response_guidance: Block the destination and isolate the source host pending investigation; treat as a confirmed C2 channel if the destination has no legitimate business purpose.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: coefficient of variation <= 0.15

title: FortiGate Long-Lived Outbound Encrypted Session
description: An outbound TLS session remains open for an unusually long duration compared to typical web-browsing sessions — consistent with a persistent reverse-shell or remote-access-tool tunnel maintained over an encrypted channel rather than a normal request/response web transaction.

data_sources.name: FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: Per-session duration for outbound TLS traffic.

detection_logic: Filters outbound HTTPS sessions with duration exceeding a configured threshold.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound" service="HTTPS"
| where duration>=3600
| table _time, srcip, dstip, duration, sentbyte, rcvdbyte
tuning_guidance: Exclude known long-lived legitimate connections (streaming, backup replication, VoIP/collaboration tools, webhook listeners).
investigation_steps: Check the byte pattern — a small, steady bidirectional trickle over a long duration is more C2-like than a large one-directional transfer.
Check destination reputation and first-seen status.
response_guidance: Investigate the source host; block the destination if no legitimate purpose is identified.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: duration >= 3600s

title: FortiGate Outbound Connection to Known Dynamic DNS Domain
description: An internal host resolves or connects to a domain under a known dynamic-DNS provider (e.g. duckdns.org, no-ip.com, dynu.com and similar). Dynamic DNS is disproportionately used by malware/C2 infrastructure because it lets an attacker rapidly repoint a stable-looking hostname to new infrastructure.
detection_logic: Matches queried/connected domains against a maintained lookup of known dynamic-DNS provider suffixes.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=dns
| lookup fgt_dyndns_providers.csv domain_suffix OUTPUT is_dyndns
| where is_dyndns="true"
| table _time, srcip, domain, action
tuning_guidance: Some legitimate remote-access/IoT products use dynamic DNS by design — maintain an allowlist for known-good uses.
investigation_steps: Check the resolved IP's reputation and any subsequent connection.
Correlate with the source host's process/endpoint telemetry if available.
response_guidance: Block the domain category via DNS filter; investigate the source host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Outbound Connection to Tor or Anonymization Service
description: An internal host connects to a known Tor entry/relay node or public VPN/anonymization proxy service. In most enterprise environments this has no legitimate business purpose and is either policy-violating user behavior or malware attempting to anonymize its C2 traffic.

data_sources.name: FortiGate traffic/application control log
data_sources.description: Connections matching known Tor/anonymizer IP ranges or application signatures.

detection_logic: Matches destination IP against a maintained Tor-node/anonymizer threat-intelligence lookup, or Application Control category 'Proxy'/'Tor'.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward
| lookup fgt_tor_nodes.csv dstip OUTPUT is_tor
| where is_tor="true"
| table _time, srcip, dstip, dstport, action
tuning_guidance: Requires a regularly-refreshed Tor exit-node list (e.g. from a threat-intel feed) — stale lists will miss current infrastructure.
investigation_steps: Determine whether Application Control already blocked the connection (action=deny) vs. allowed it.
Investigate the source host for malware if the connection was not user-initiated browser traffic.
response_guidance: Block Tor/anonymizer categories via Application Control if not already enforced; investigate the source host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Outbound SSH Tunneling to Unusual Destination
description: An internal host (not a designated administrative jump host) establishes an outbound SSH connection to an external, previously-unseen destination — a common vector for SSH-based tunneling/port-forwarding used to bypass egress controls or establish a covert channel.
detection_logic: Filters outbound port-22 connections from hosts not on the known-SSH-client allowlist to external destinations.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound" dstport=22 action="accept"
| lookup fgt_ssh_allowed_sources.csv srcip OUTPUT is_allowed
| where isnull(is_allowed)
| table _time, srcip, dstip, duration, sentbyte, rcvdbyte
tuning_guidance: Maintain the allowlist of hosts with a legitimate business reason for outbound SSH (CI/CD, automation, designated jump hosts).
investigation_steps: Check session duration/byte pattern for tunneling-consistent behavior (long-lived, bidirectional).
Investigate the source host.
response_guidance: Block outbound SSH from non-designated hosts at the perimeter policy level; investigate confirmed unauthorized use.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate DNS Tunneling Indicators (High Query Volume / Long Labels / Encoded Subdomains)
description: A source host generates a high volume of DNS queries with unusually long labels, high-entropy/base32/base64-like subdomains, or against a single unusual parent domain — the classic fingerprint of DNS tunneling tools used for C2 or data exfiltration through a channel that is rarely fully inspected.

data_sources.name: FortiGate DNS filter log
data_sources.description: DNS query records with queried hostname and source.

detection_logic: Computes query volume per source/domain in a rolling window and flags combinations of high volume, long average label length, and high subdomain entropy.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=dns
| eval label_len=len(domain)
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as query_count, avg(label_len) as avg_label_len, dc(domain) as distinct_subdomains by srcip, _time
| where query_count>=100 AND avg_label_len>=40
tuning_guidance: Exclude known legitimate high-volume DNS consumers (recursive resolvers, CDN health checks); entropy scoring on the subdomain label (not shown here) meaningfully reduces false positives if implemented via a lookup-based scoring function.
investigation_steps: Identify the parent domain queried and check its reputation/registration age.
Inspect a sample of the actual subdomain labels for encoded-data patterns.
response_guidance: Block the domain at the DNS filter; investigate the source host for a tunneling tool/malware.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: avg label length >= 40 chars

title: FortiGate NXDOMAIN Query Burst
description: A source host generates an unusually high rate of DNS queries that resolve to NXDOMAIN (non-existent domain) in a short window — consistent with a Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) probing a sequence of algorithmically-generated candidate C2 domains, most of which are not yet (or never) registered.

data_sources.name: FortiGate DNS filter log
data_sources.description: DNS query results including NXDOMAIN responses.

detection_logic: Counts NXDOMAIN-resulting queries per source host in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=dns rcode="NXDOMAIN"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as nxdomain_count, dc(domain) as distinct_domains by srcip, _time
| where nxdomain_count>=30
tuning_guidance: Exclude hosts running legitimate domain-generation-heavy software (some ad-blockers, threat-intel tools, misconfigured search-domain suffix lists cause repeated NXDOMAIN too).
investigation_steps: Sample the queried domain names for DGA-like patterns (random-looking, consistent length).
Investigate the source host for malware.
response_guidance: Investigate and remediate the source host; consider DNS-based sinkholing for confirmed DGA activity.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1568.002: Domain Generation Algorithms

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate DNS Resolver Configuration Changed
description: The device's own DNS resolver settings, or DNS filter profile applied to policies, are changed — including disabling DNS filtering entirely or pointing resolution at an unfamiliar server. Duplicates part of FGT-050's system-DNS coverage but focused specifically on the DNS Filter security-profile angle rather than base system configuration.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under dnsfilter.profile, particularly disabling of botnet-C2/malicious categories.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="dnsfilter.profile"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr, action
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during profile tuning; flag specifically when the botnet-C2 or malicious-domain category is disabled.
investigation_steps: Confirm which categories were affected.
Check for a subsequent increase in queries to categories that were previously blocked.
response_guidance: Re-enable the affected categories unless explicitly justified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Critical IPS Signature Triggered
description: FortiGuard IPS detects a critical-severity signature match. Whether the action taken was block or allow (see FGT-081 for that distinction), a critical IPS hit represents FortiGuard's own threat-intelligence-backed assessment that the traffic matches a known exploit pattern.

data_sources.name: FortiGate IPS log
data_sources.description: IPS signature matches with severity, action, source, and destination.

detection_logic: Filters IPS log for severity=critical events.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=ips severity="critical"
| table _time, srcip, dstip, attack, action, proto, service
tuning_guidance: Individually low-noise given the critical-only filter; validate signature relevance against actual deployed software (an IPS hit for a product you don't run is lower priority).
investigation_steps: Check the action field — allowed critical hits require immediate investigation (FGT-081).
Identify the targeted service/host and its patch status.
response_guidance: Investigate the destination host for signs of successful exploitation regardless of blocked/allowed status.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate IPS Signature Matched but Traffic Allowed
description: An IPS signature matches traffic, but the configured action for that policy/signature is monitor-only or pass rather than block/reset. This means an exploit attempt reached its target uninterrupted — the single highest-priority IPS scenario, since detection without prevention means the follow-on impact must be assumed until ruled out.

data_sources.name: FortiGate IPS log
data_sources.description: IPS matches where the resulting action did not block the traffic.

detection_logic: Filters IPS log for events where action is pass or monitor rather than block/reset/dropped.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=ips (action="pass" OR action="monitor")
| table _time, srcip, dstip, attack, severity, service
tuning_guidance: If a large fraction of your IPS sensor is in monitor mode by design (staged rollout), this will be high-volume — prioritize critical/high severity within the allowed set.
investigation_steps: Assume the exploit succeeded and investigate the destination host directly (process activity, new accounts, outbound connections).
Check whether this destination is also flagged in FortiEDR/FortiClient telemetry if deployed.
response_guidance: Move the relevant IPS sensor to block mode for this signature class; investigate the destination host as a potential compromise.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Repeated IPS Exploit Attempts From Same Source
description: A single source IP triggers multiple distinct IPS signatures, or the same signature repeatedly, against one or more targets within a short window — consistent with an attacker running an exploit framework/scanner that attempts several exploit chains in sequence rather than a single opportunistic hit.

data_sources.name: FortiGate IPS log
data_sources.description: IPS matches by source and signature.

detection_logic: Counts IPS events per source IP in a rolling window, regardless of destination.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=ips
| bin _time span=15m
| stats count, dc(attack) as distinct_signatures, dc(dstip) as distinct_targets, values(attack) as signatures by srcip, _time
| where count>=10 OR distinct_targets>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude authorized internal vulnerability-scanning/pentest source ranges during scheduled assessment windows.
investigation_steps: List the signatures triggered and cross-reference against exploited products in your environment.
Check whether any allowed (non-blocked) hits occurred among them (FGT-081).
response_guidance: Block the source IP at the perimeter; investigate targeted hosts for signs of compromise.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate IPS Exploit Followed by Outbound Command-and-Control Connection
description: An IPS exploit hit against a specific internal host is followed, within a short window, by that same host initiating an unusual outbound connection (new destination, beaconing pattern, or a threat-intel-flagged IP). This chains exploitation to its most likely next stage and is one of the highest-confidence indicators in the entire traffic-analytics section.

data_sources.name: FortiGate IPS + traffic log
data_sources.description: IPS hit against a host followed by that host's own outbound connections.

detection_logic: Correlates an IPS event where dstip=host with a subsequent outbound connection where srcip=host to a new/rare destination, within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=ips
| eval victim=dstip, stage="1_exploited"
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound"
  | lookup fgt_dest_baseline.csv srcip dstip OUTPUT is_known
  | where isnull(is_known)
  | eval victim=srcip, stage="2_new_outbound" ]
| transaction victim maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_exploited")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, victim, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-host destination baseline (fgt_dest_baseline.csv) for the 'new outbound' stage to be meaningful; without it this will over-fire on any exploited host's normal traffic.
investigation_steps: Treat as a likely successful compromise.
Isolate the affected host immediately and begin endpoint investigation if FortiEDR/FortiClient telemetry is available.
response_guidance: Isolate the host, block the outbound destination, and initiate incident response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: IPS exploit hit -> new/rare outbound connection from same host

title: FortiGate IPS Bypass or IPS Profile Removed From Public-Facing Policy
description: An IPS sensor is removed from, or its enforcement mode weakened on, a policy that serves Internet-facing traffic. A special case of FGT-034 called out separately because IPS is frequently the last line of defense for a publicly-exposed service and its removal deserves its own dedicated, unambiguous alert.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: IPS sensor attachment changes on Internet-facing policies.

detection_logic: Filters policy edits removing the ips-sensor attribute, joined against a lookup of policies serving WAN-facing traffic.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" cfgattr="ips-sensor"
| lookup fgt_internet_facing_policies.csv cfgobj OUTPUT is_internet_facing
| where is_internet_facing="true"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Maintain the Internet-facing-policy lookup; regenerate it whenever new inbound VIPs/policies are approved (FGT-027/FGT-036).
investigation_steps: Re-attach the IPS sensor immediately if unauthorized.
Check for exploit attempts against the now-uninspected policy in the intervening window.
response_guidance: Treat as Critical; restore protection immediately and audit traffic during the exposure window.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Malware Detected and Blocked
description: FortiGate's antivirus engine identifies and blocks a known-malicious file in transit. Successfully blocked malware is the expected, working-as-intended case but still worth tracking to identify targeted users/hosts and repeated exposure.

data_sources.name: FortiGate antivirus log
data_sources.description: Antivirus detections with verdict, hash, and action.

detection_logic: Filters antivirus log for blocked detections.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=virus action="blocked"
| table _time, srcip, dstip, user, virus, filename, quarskip
tuning_guidance: Track by user/host to identify repeat targets warranting user security awareness follow-up.
investigation_steps: Identify the delivery vector (web download, email attachment via FortiMail if integrated).
response_guidance: No emergency action for a successfully blocked detection; escalate if the same hash appears across multiple hosts (FGT-087).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Malware Detected but Allowed Through
description: Antivirus identifies malware but the configured action allows the file through (monitor-only profile, or a policy without full antivirus scanning applied). The destination host has received a known-malicious file — assume execution and investigate accordingly.

data_sources.name: FortiGate antivirus log
data_sources.description: Antivirus detections that were not blocked.

detection_logic: Filters antivirus log for detections where action is not blocked.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=virus (action="allowed" OR action="monitored")
| table _time, srcip, dstip, user, virus, filename
tuning_guidance: Any occurrence warrants review — this profile combination is itself a finding independent of the specific malware.
investigation_steps: Immediately investigate the destination host for execution artifacts.
If FortiEDR/FortiClient is deployed on the host, check for a corresponding endpoint detection.
response_guidance: Isolate the destination host and treat as a likely infection pending endpoint verification; move the relevant policy to full block mode.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Same Malware Hash Detected Across Multiple Hosts
description: The same file hash is detected by antivirus across multiple distinct internal hosts within a short window — consistent with a self-propagating threat, a shared malicious download source (e.g. a compromised internal file share), or a targeted campaign delivering the same payload broadly.
detection_logic: Counts distinct destination hosts per detected hash/virus name in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=virus
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(dstip) as distinct_hosts, values(dstip) as hosts by virus, _time
| where distinct_hosts>=3
tuning_guidance: Common, expected pattern for signature-database-driven mass detections of widely-circulating commodity malware — cross-reference against known outbreak advisories before treating as targeted.
investigation_steps: Identify the common delivery source (shared download link, compromised internal share, phishing campaign).
Check FortiSandbox verdict if the file was submitted (FSB-### detections).
response_guidance: Contain the common source; sweep all affected hosts for the hash.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Antivirus Profile Bypass or Disabled on Policy
description: An antivirus profile is removed from, or set to a weaker inspection mode (e.g. flow-based to quick scan only) on, a firewall policy. Documented separately from the general FGT-034 security-profile-removal detection because antivirus is the layer most directly responsible for catching known malicious file transfers.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Antivirus profile attachment/mode changes on policies.

detection_logic: Filters policy edits where cfgattr=av-profile and the value is removed or weakened.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.policy" cfgattr="av-profile"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Correlate with FGT-034 to avoid double-alerting on the same underlying change; this is a specialization for teams that want AV-specific routing.
investigation_steps: Re-attach or restore full inspection mode if unauthorized.
response_guidance: Restore antivirus inspection immediately for Internet-facing or high-risk policies.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Remote Access or Tunneling Application Detected
description: Application Control identifies traffic matching a remote-access tool (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, ScreenConnect and similar), tunneling utility, or unsanctioned VPN client signature. These legitimate dual-use tools are heavily favored by attackers for hands-on-keyboard remote access because they blend into normal remote-support traffic and are frequently allowlisted.

data_sources.name: FortiGate application control log
data_sources.description: Application signature matches with category and action.

detection_logic: Filters application control log for the Remote.Access and Proxy application categories.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=app-ctrl (appcat="Remote.Access" OR appcat="Proxy" OR appcat="Tunneling")
| table _time, srcip, dstip, user, app, action
tuning_guidance: Maintain an allowlist of IT-sanctioned remote-support tools/hosts; alert only on unsanctioned tools or sanctioned tools used by unexpected hosts/users.
investigation_steps: Confirm the tool and destination against sanctioned IT support usage.
If unsanctioned, investigate the source host for how the tool was installed.
response_guidance: Block unsanctioned remote-access application categories; investigate confirmed unauthorized use as a potential hands-on-keyboard intrusion.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1219: Remote Access Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Cryptomining Application or Protocol Detected
description: Application Control identifies a cryptomining application/protocol signature (Stratum mining protocol, known mining-pool traffic). Nearly always indicates unauthorized software on the source host, whether installed by an insider or dropped by malware monetizing a compromised host.
detection_logic: Filters application control log for the Cryptomining category.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=app-ctrl appcat="Cryptomining"
| table _time, srcip, dstip, user, app, action
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate business case in most environments — treat every occurrence as worth investigating.
investigation_steps: Identify the source host and process responsible.
Check for related IPS/AV detections on the same host.
response_guidance: Isolate the host and remove the mining software; investigate for a broader compromise given mining payloads are frequently dropped as a secondary/opportunistic payload.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Unsanctioned Cloud Storage or File-Sharing Application Detected
description: Application Control identifies traffic to a cloud-storage/file-sharing service outside the organization's sanctioned platform (e.g. a personal Dropbox/Mega/file-sharing account when the org standardizes on a different provider). A common exfiltration path since it blends into normal-looking HTTPS traffic to a reputable cloud provider.
detection_logic: Filters application control log for cloud-storage categories not on the sanctioned-application allowlist.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=app-ctrl (appcat="Cloud.IT" OR appcat="Storage.Backup")
| lookup fgt_sanctioned_apps.csv app OUTPUT is_sanctioned
| where isnull(is_sanctioned)
| table _time, srcip, user, app, action
tuning_guidance: Maintain the sanctioned-application allowlist; this is a high-volume, low-severity signal best used as an enrichment input for the exfiltration correlation detections.
investigation_steps: Check upload volume associated with the session (correlate with FGT-071).
response_guidance: Block unsanctioned categories via policy if data-loss risk is a concern for the affected user group.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567.002: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Web Filter Blocks Malware, Phishing, or C2 Category
description: FortiGuard Web Filter categorizes and blocks a request to a site tagged malware, phishing, or command-and-control. Confirms the source host attempted to reach known-bad infrastructure, whether via user click or automated malware behavior.

data_sources.name: FortiGate web filter log
data_sources.description: Web filter category matches and action taken.

detection_logic: Filters web filter log for the Malicious Websites, Phishing, and Command and Control categories.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=webfilter (catdesc="Malicious Websites" OR catdesc="Phishing" OR catdesc="Command and Control")
| table _time, srcip, user, url, catdesc, action
tuning_guidance: Expected background rate from user misclicks on phishing links; escalate on repeated attempts from the same host (FGT-093) or any allowed (non-blocked) hit.
investigation_steps: Check whether the request was blocked or allowed.
For C2-category hits specifically, treat as higher priority than phishing (more likely to reflect active malware, not a user click).
response_guidance: No emergency action for a single blocked hit; investigate the host directly for a C2-category hit.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated FortiGate Web Filter Blocks From Same Host
description: A single internal host generates multiple malicious/phishing/C2-category web-filter blocks within a short window — more consistent with an infected host repeatedly attempting to reach its C2 (retrying on failure) than a single user click.

data_sources.name: FortiGate web filter log
data_sources.description: Web filter category matches by source host.

detection_logic: Counts malicious-category web-filter blocks per source host in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=webfilter (catdesc="Malicious Websites" OR catdesc="Phishing" OR catdesc="Command and Control")
| bin _time span=15m
| stats count, values(url) as urls by srcip, user, _time
| where count>=3
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive rate given the malicious-category prefilter; suitable as a page-worthy alert in most environments.
investigation_steps: Isolate and investigate the host for malware.
Check whether the domain pattern is consistent across attempts (single C2 vs. varied phishing clicks).
response_guidance: Isolate the host; treat as a likely active infection.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Web Filter Category Override Added
description: A URL/category override is added to the web filter configuration, allowing traffic to a specific site that would otherwise be blocked by category. Legitimate for business-need exceptions, but also a mechanism to quietly whitelist an attacker-controlled domain past the web filter.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under webfilter.override and webfilter.urlfilter for new allow entries.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system (cfgpath="webfilter.override" OR cfgpath="webfilter.urlfilter")
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, action
tuning_guidance: Require a business justification/change ticket for every override; review the override list quarterly for stale or suspicious entries.
investigation_steps: Check the domain's reputation and registration age.
Confirm business justification with the requesting user/team.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized overrides.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate SSL Deep Inspection Disabled or Exemption Added
description: SSL/SSH deep inspection is disabled (falling back to certificate-inspection-only, which cannot see inside the encrypted payload), or a new destination/category exemption is added to the SSL inspection profile. Since the large majority of both legitimate and malicious traffic is now encrypted, this single control determines whether IPS/AV/DLP/Application Control can actually see what's inside most sessions.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events under firewall.ssl-ssh-profile for inspection-mode downgrades or new exempt-list entries.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.ssl-ssh-profile"
| table _time, devname, user, cfgobj, cfgattr, action
tuning_guidance: Certificate-pinned applications (some banking/collaboration apps) legitimately require exemptions — maintain a reviewed exemption list rather than broad SSL-inspection bypass.
investigation_steps: Identify the specific exemption/downgrade and its scope (single destination vs. entire profile).
Assess what other security-profile inspection now loses visibility as a result.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes; restore full deep inspection for Internet-facing and general-browsing policies.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate SSL Certificate Validation Error or Weak/Obsolete TLS Observed
description: SSL inspection logs a certificate validation failure (untrusted CA, expired, self-signed, hostname mismatch) or negotiation of an obsolete TLS version/cipher on an outbound connection. A meaningful fraction of malware C2 infrastructure uses self-signed or otherwise invalid certificates, making this a useful (if noisy) enrichment signal.

data_sources.name: FortiGate SSL log
data_sources.description: SSL/TLS session inspection results including certificate validation outcome and negotiated protocol version.

detection_logic: Filters SSL inspection log for certificate validation failures on outbound sessions.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=ssl direction="outbound" (action="blocked" OR reason="*cert*")
| table _time, srcip, dstip, reason, action
tuning_guidance: High background rate from internal tooling and self-signed internal services reached over odd paths — best combined with a rare-destination filter rather than used standalone.
investigation_steps: Correlate with FGT-070/FGT-072 for a first-seen or beaconing destination.
response_guidance: No standalone action; feeds C2 correlation detections.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiGate Large Outbound File Transfer via FTP, SFTP, or SCP
description: A large outbound file transfer occurs via FTP, SFTP, or SCP to an external destination. These protocols are less commonly used for routine outbound traffic than HTTPS, so a large transfer over them is a stronger exfiltration signal than the general byte-volume anomaly in FGT-071.
detection_logic: Filters outbound FTP/SFTP/SCP sessions where sentbyte exceeds a configured threshold.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound" (service="FTP" OR (dstport=22 AND app="SCP"))
| where sentbyte>=104857600
| table _time, srcip, dstip, service, sentbyte
tuning_guidance: Exclude known backup/replication jobs using these protocols to an approved external destination (e.g. an offsite DR target).
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the transfer.
Identify what data was on the source host.
response_guidance: Block if unauthorized and investigate the source host for compromise.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048.003: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: sentbyte >= 100MB

title: FortiGate Off-Hours Large Outbound Data Transfer
description: A large outbound data transfer (any protocol) occurs outside business hours — a classic pattern for insider or compromised-account exfiltration timed to avoid observation, and a higher-confidence variant of FGT-071 when combined with off-hours timing.

data_sources.name: FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: Outbound session byte counts with timestamp.

detection_logic: Filters large outbound sessions where the hour-of-day/day-of-week falls outside business hours.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound"
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H"), dow=strftime(_time,"%a")
| where sentbyte>=104857600 AND ((hour<"06" OR hour>="22") OR dow=="Sat" OR dow=="Sun")
| table _time, srcip, dstip, sentbyte, hour, dow
tuning_guidance: Exclude scheduled off-hours backup jobs explicitly by source host.
investigation_steps: Identify the user/host and destination.
Check whether this correlates with a VPN session outside normal hours (FGT-056).
response_guidance: Investigate as potential exfiltration; contact the account owner to confirm legitimacy.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: sentbyte >= 100MB, outside business hours

title: FortiGate DNS-Based Data Exfiltration Volume Threshold
description: Cumulative DNS query volume and payload-encoded label volume from a single host crosses a threshold consistent with meaningful data exfiltration over DNS (as opposed to the lighter-weight tunneling/beaconing signature in FGT-077) — i.e. sustained high-volume DNS traffic that, if each query is carrying encoded data, would represent a non-trivial amount of exfiltrated content.

data_sources.name: FortiGate DNS filter log
data_sources.description: DNS query volume by source host.

detection_logic: Sums estimated bytes-per-query (based on label length) per source host over an extended window and flags totals exceeding a data-volume threshold.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=dns
| eval est_bytes=len(domain)
| bin _time span=1h
| stats sum(est_bytes) as est_total_bytes, count as query_count by srcip, _time
| where est_total_bytes>=5000000
tuning_guidance: This is a coarse estimate (DNS labels are capped at 63 bytes/253 total, so the calculation is illustrative) — pair with FGT-077's entropy/volume signal for higher-confidence alerting.
investigation_steps: Correlate with FGT-077 for the specific tunneling indicators.
Identify the parent domain and its infrastructure.
response_guidance: Block the domain; investigate the source host for a tunneling tool.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: estimated >= 5MB/hour of DNS label volume from one host

title: FortiManager Administrator Login Failure
description: A single failed FortiManager administrator login. FortiManager sits above the entire managed FortiGate fleet, so authentication events against it carry proportionally higher stakes than a single FortiGate's own admin logins — this is the atomic building block for the threshold/sequence detections below.
detection_logic: Filters FortiManager event log for administrative login failures.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system action="login" status="failed"
| table _time, user, srcip, reason
tuning_guidance: Expect routine noise; use FMG-002/003 for volume-based alerting.
investigation_steps: Confirm srcip is a known management source.
response_guidance: No action for an isolated failure.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated FortiManager Administrator Login Failures / Brute Force
description: Five or more failed FortiManager login attempts within 10 minutes. Given that FortiManager compromise can cascade to every managed FortiGate, this deserves a lower alert threshold and higher default severity than the equivalent single-device FortiGate detection (FGT-002).
detection_logic: Counts failed FortiManager admin logins in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system action="login" status="failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, dc(user) as distinct_users, values(srcip) as source_ips by _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Minimal legitimate tuning expected given how rarely FortiManager should see failed-login bursts.
investigation_steps: Identify targeted usernames and validate them.
Check for a subsequent success (FMG-004).
response_guidance: Block the source IP; this is Tier-0 infrastructure — treat with urgency comparable to a domain controller.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Login From Unusual Administrator or Source
description: A successful FortiManager login from a source IP or by an administrator account not seen in the prior 30 days. Given FortiManager's small, typically-static set of legitimate operators, first-seen events here are unusually high-signal compared to the same pattern on an individual FortiGate.
detection_logic: Builds a 30-day baseline of (user, srcip) pairs and flags first-seen combinations.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system action="login" status="success"
| lookup fmg_admin_ip_baseline.csv user srcip OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, srcip
tuning_guidance: Maintain fmg_admin_ip_baseline.csv via a nightly scheduled search rather than the inline subsearch pattern used elsewhere, given the low event volume on this system.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the administrator directly.
Review the session's activity in full given FortiManager's blast radius.
response_guidance: Suspend the session pending confirmation if unexpected.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful FortiManager Login Following Repeated Failures
description: A successful FortiManager login for a user/source that had five or more failures in the preceding 30 minutes. Given that FortiManager compromise is a direct path to fleet-wide FortiGate compromise, this is one of the two or three highest-priority detections across the entire Fortinet catalogue.
detection_logic: Joins a failed-login threshold with a subsequent success for the same user within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system action="login"
| eval outcome=if(status="failed","fail","success")
| transaction user maxspan=30m startswith=eval(outcome="fail") endswith=eval(outcome="success")
| where eventcount>=6
| table _time, user, srcip, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low false-positive rate expected given FortiManager's typically small, well-known administrator population.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately review the session for any device, policy-package, or script activity (FMG-020+).
response_guidance: Suspend the account, disconnect the session, and audit every managed FortiGate for changes originating from this session before doing anything else.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager API Login From Unusual Source
description: A JSON-RPC API session against FortiManager is authenticated from a source not on the known-automation allowlist. FortiManager's API is the interface most orchestration/automation tooling uses to push fleet-wide changes, making it an equally attractive target for an attacker seeking the same fleet-wide reach without an interactive GUI session.
detection_logic: Filters API-session login events against a known-automation-source allowlist.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*JSON-RPC*"
| lookup fmg_api_allowed_sources.csv srcip OUTPUT is_allowed
| where isnull(is_allowed)
| table _time, user, srcip
tuning_guidance: Maintain the automation-source allowlist for CI/CD, orchestration, and integration platforms.
investigation_steps: Confirm the API session's origin and scope of actions taken.
response_guidance: Revoke and reissue API credentials if the source is unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New FortiManager Administrator Created
description: A new local administrator account is created on FortiManager. Given FortiManager's role as central management infrastructure, this deserves the same treatment as a new domain-admin account in Active Directory.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for administrator object creation.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*admin*added*"
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: Correlate with change tickets for legitimate onboarding.
investigation_steps: Verify against approved accounts list.
Check the profile/permission level assigned.
response_guidance: Disable immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Administrator Granted Super_User Profile
description: An administrator is granted the Super_User profile, FortiManager's highest privilege level, capable of managing every ADOM, device, and policy package in the deployment.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for profile changes to Super_User.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*profile*" msg="*Super_User*"
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning — every occurrence should map to a change record.
investigation_steps: Verify against change management.
Review what the account does immediately afterward.
response_guidance: Downgrade immediately if unauthorized; treat as Critical management-plane-compromise indicator.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Administrator Trusted Hosts Changed
description: An administrator's trusted-hosts restriction is removed or broadened, the same class of high-consequence change as FGT-016 but on the system that manages the entire fleet.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for trusted-hosts attribute changes.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*trusthost*"
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate ongoing pattern.
investigation_steps: Identify who made the change and cross-reference against a change ticket.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Remote Authentication (RADIUS/LDAP) Configuration Changed
description: The centralized authentication server configuration used by FortiManager administrators is modified — the FortiManager-level equivalent of FGT-019, with proportionally larger impact given how many downstream FortiGates depend on the integrity of this single control plane.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for RADIUS/LDAP server configuration changes.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*radius*" OR msg="*ldap*") (msg="*server*" OR msg="*secret*")
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned identity-infrastructure migrations; require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Verify the new server address is known and owned.
Audit all logins since the change.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unauthorized or Unexpected FortiGate Device Registered to FortiManager
description: A new FortiGate device is registered/added to FortiManager management. A rogue device registration could let an attacker pull configuration/policy data intended for legitimate devices, or (more subtly) let a legitimate-looking device receive fleet-wide policy pushes intended for trusted infrastructure.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for device-addition events, cross-referenced against a known-asset inventory.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*device*added*"
| lookup fmg_known_assets.csv serial OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, devname, serial
tuning_guidance: Maintain fmg_known_assets.csv as the authoritative asset inventory; sync from procurement/CMDB where possible.
investigation_steps: Verify the device serial number against procurement records.
Confirm the registering administrator.
response_guidance: Deregister immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Device Removed From Management
description: A device is deregistered/removed from FortiManager management. Removes it from centralized policy enforcement and audit visibility — an attacker who has separately compromised a FortiGate may remove it from FortiManager first to stop configuration drift from being detected centrally.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for device-removal events.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*device*deleted*"
| table _time, user, devname
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned decommissioning.
investigation_steps: Confirm against decommissioning records.
response_guidance: Investigate if unaccounted for; verify the device's own local configuration was not tampered with immediately before removal.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Device Reassigned Between ADOMs
description: A managed device is moved between Administrative Domains (ADOMs). ADOMs are typically used to segregate customer or business-unit environments within a shared FortiManager — moving a device between them can expose it to a different policy package/administrator population than intended.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for ADOM reassignment events.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*ADOM*" msg="*mov*"
| table _time, user, devname, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during org restructuring; require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm the destination ADOM's administrator population and policy package are appropriate for this device.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Policy Package Modified
description: A centrally-managed policy package is edited. This is the FortiManager-level equivalent of a FortiGate policy edit (FGT-030), except a single edit here can affect every device the package is assigned to once installed — the baseline detection for the higher-severity fleet-wide install detections that follow.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for policy package modification events.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*policy package*" (msg="*edit*" OR msg="*modif*")
| table _time, user, pkgname, msg
tuning_guidance: High-frequency in change-managed environments; rely on FMG-014/015/016 for alerting.
investigation_steps: Identify what changed and which devices the package is assigned to.
response_guidance: No automatic action; feeds downstream detections.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Mass Configuration Push to Many FortiGates
description: A single install operation deploys a policy package or configuration change to an unusually large number of FortiGates at once. This is exactly the fleet-wide blast-radius scenario the master specification calls out as the Fortinet equivalent of the AAP/Satellite management-plane problem: one compromised (or reckless) FortiManager action can reconfigure the entire perimeter simultaneously.

data_sources.name: FortiManager event log
data_sources.description: Install task events with target device count.

detection_logic: Counts distinct target devices per install task and flags installs above a fleet-percentage threshold.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*install*"
| rex field=msg "(?<device_count>\d+)\s+device"
| where device_count>=10
| table _time, user, pkgname, device_count
tuning_guidance: Baseline your organization's normal install scope (some environments legitimately push to the entire fleet routinely) and tune the threshold to what is actually anomalous for you.
investigation_steps: Verify against a change ticket for the deployment.
Diff the pushed change for any security-control weakening (FMG-015).
response_guidance: If unauthorized, this is a fleet-wide incident: halt further installs, identify every affected device, and prepare to roll back.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Deployment Weakens Security Controls Fleet-Wide
description: A policy package install that removes or disables security profiles, logging, or IPS across its target devices — the fleet-wide analogue of FGT-034/FGT-040/FGT-041, and the single most damaging outcome this catalogue defends against on the FortiManager side, since it can silently blind the entire managed estate at once.

data_sources.name: FortiManager event log
data_sources.description: Policy package content changes cross-referenced with install events.

detection_logic: Correlates a policy-package edit that removes a security-profile/logging attribute with a subsequent install of that package.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system
| eval stage=case(msg="*policy package*" AND (cfgattr="ips-sensor" OR cfgattr="av-profile" OR cfgattr="logtraffic") AND msg="*remov*","1_control_removed", msg="*install*","2_installed", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction pkgname maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_control_removed")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, pkgname, stage
tuning_guidance: Validate the cfgattr/msg keyword matching against your actual FortiManager version's log format before enabling as a paging alert.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live fleet-wide incident.
Identify every device the package was installed to.
Restore the removed controls and reinstall immediately.
response_guidance: Halt further deployment, restore security controls fleet-wide, and audit for unauthorized traffic on every affected device during the exposure window.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: control removed from package -> package installed

title: FortiManager Deployment Outside Change Window or by Unusual Administrator
description: An install/deployment task runs outside the organization's declared change window, or is initiated by an administrator account not typically associated with deployment activity.

data_sources.name: FortiManager event log
data_sources.description: Install task events with initiating user and timestamp.

detection_logic: Cross-references install events against a change-window lookup and a deployment-authorized-users lookup.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*install*"
| lookup fmg_change_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| lookup fmg_deployment_admins.csv user OUTPUT is_deployment_admin
| where isnull(in_window) OR isnull(is_deployment_admin)
| table _time, user, pkgname
tuning_guidance: Maintain both lookups; without them this degrades to a high-volume, low-precision alert.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket.
Verify the administrator's authorization to perform deployments.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed; treat as a potential compromised-session indicator.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager CLI Script Created or Modified
description: A CLI script object is created or modified in FortiManager's script repository. Scripts are arbitrary CLI command sequences that can be run against one or many managed devices — functionally equivalent to the AAP/Ansible playbook problem in the Red Hat catalogue, and deserving the same elevated scrutiny.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for script object create/edit events.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*script*" (msg="*creat*" OR msg="*modif*")
| table _time, user, scriptname, msg
tuning_guidance: Correlate with change management; review script content for security-relevant commands (FMG-019).
investigation_steps: Review the full script content for suspicious commands.
Identify the intended target scope.
response_guidance: Review before allowing execution; delete if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Script Executed Across Multiple FortiGates
description: A CLI script is run against multiple managed FortiGates in a single execution. Scripts execute arbitrary CLI commands with the FortiManager service account's effective authority on the target device — a script run fleet-wide is one of the most powerful single actions available anywhere in the Security Fabric.

data_sources.name: FortiManager event log
data_sources.description: Script execution events with target device count.

detection_logic: Filters script execution events where the target device count exceeds a threshold.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*script*" msg="*run*"
| rex field=msg "(?<device_count>\d+)\s+device"
| where device_count>=5
| table _time, user, scriptname, device_count
tuning_guidance: Baseline your organization's normal script-execution scope; some environments legitimately run maintenance scripts fleet-wide on a schedule (allowlist those specific script names).
investigation_steps: Immediately review the executed script content.
Identify every affected device.
response_guidance: Treat as a live incident if unauthorized: audit every affected device for the exact commands executed and revert.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Script Contains Suspicious or Security-Control-Impairing Commands
description: A CLI script's content includes commands that disable logging, remove security profiles, create administrator accounts, or otherwise weaken security controls. Content-based detection on the script body itself, complementing the execution-count-based FMG-018.

data_sources.name: FortiManager event log
data_sources.description: Script body content compared against a suspicious-command pattern list.

detection_logic: Matches script content against patterns for admin creation, logging disable, security-profile removal, or firewall policy changes.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_scripts
| regex script_content="(config system admin|set log.*disable|unset (ips-sensor|av-profile)|config firewall policy)"
| table _time, user, scriptname
tuning_guidance: Requires the script repository content to be indexed (via a scheduled API pull if not natively logged) — validate this data source is actually available in your deployment before relying on it.
investigation_steps: Review the full script and its intended target scope before it executes if caught pre-execution.
If already executed, treat per FMG-018/FMG-015.
response_guidance: Block execution and review with the script's author; delete if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Configuration Rollback or Revision Restore
description: A device's configuration is rolled back to a prior revision via FortiManager. Can undo recent legitimate hardening, or (used by an attacker) restore a prior configuration that lacks recently-added security controls without the change being individually visible as a series of edits.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for revision restore/rollback events.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*revision*" (msg="*restor*" OR msg="*rollback*")
| table _time, user, devname, revision
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned rollback of a bad change; require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Diff the restored revision against the current configuration to identify exactly what changed.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized rollbacks.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601.002: Downgrade System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager Device Configuration Retrieved or Exported
description: A managed device's full configuration is retrieved/exported from FortiManager. Since FortiManager holds configuration (and configuration-referenced secret material) for every device it manages, bulk or repeated retrieval is a meaningful collection signal — potentially exposing far more than a single-device export (FGT-043/044) would.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for configuration retrieval/export events, counting distinct devices retrieved per user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system msg="*config*retriev*"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(devname) as distinct_devices, values(devname) as devices by user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=5
tuning_guidance: Expected for scheduled backup automation — allowlist the known automation account and alert on other actors.
investigation_steps: Confirm the retrieving account and business justification.
Check whether the retrieved configurations were subsequently transferred off-platform.
response_guidance: Investigate as potential mass configuration/credential collection if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1005: Data from Local System

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiManager ADOM Database Backup or Import
description: A full ADOM or FortiManager database backup is taken, or a database is imported/restored. The most comprehensive possible data-collection event on the platform — a full backup contains every managed device's configuration history.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for database backup/import events.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*database*backup*" OR msg="*database*import*")
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: Expected for scheduled DR backups — allowlist the automation account.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for any manual/interactive backup or import.
response_guidance: Investigate unusual actors; verify the destination of any exported backup file.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1005: Data from Local System

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAnalyzer Administrator Login Failure / Brute Force
description: Repeated failed administrator login attempts against FortiAnalyzer. FortiAnalyzer holds the organization's centralized security log archive — compromising it doesn't just grant configuration control, it grants an attacker read access to (and potential ability to delete) the evidence needed to detect and investigate everything else in this catalogue.
detection_logic: Counts failed FortiAnalyzer admin logins in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system action="login" status="failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, values(srcip) as source_ips by user, _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Minimal legitimate tuning expected given the small, well-known administrator population typical of a centralized log platform.
investigation_steps: Validate targeted usernames.
Check for a subsequent success.
response_guidance: Block the source; treat with the same urgency as SIEM/log-platform compromise anywhere else in the environment.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful FortiAnalyzer Administrator Login Following Repeated Failures
description: A successful FortiAnalyzer login following a burst of failures — given FortiAnalyzer's role as the organization's centralized security evidence store, this ranks alongside FMG-004 as one of the highest-priority authentication detections in the catalogue.
detection_logic: Joins a failed-login threshold with a subsequent success for the same user within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system action="login"
| eval outcome=if(status="failed","fail","success")
| transaction user maxspan=30m startswith=eval(outcome="fail") endswith=eval(outcome="success")
| where eventcount>=6
| table _time, user, srcip, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately check for log-deletion/retention/forwarding changes (FAZ-005 through FAZ-008) made during the session.
response_guidance: Suspend the account, disconnect the session, and verify log integrity before doing anything else — a compromised FortiAnalyzer session may have deleted or redirected the very logs needed to investigate the rest of the incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New FortiAnalyzer Administrator Created or Role Changed
description: A new administrator account is created on FortiAnalyzer, or an existing account's role/permission level is elevated. Since FortiAnalyzer administrators can typically view (and in many roles, purge) the full log archive, this is a Tier-0 identity-management event.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for administrator creation or role-assignment events.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system msg="*admin*" (msg="*creat*" OR msg="*role*")
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning — correlate against change management.
investigation_steps: Verify against approved accounts.
Review the account's subsequent activity.
response_guidance: Disable/downgrade immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAnalyzer Device or Log Source Removed
description: A registered log source (a FortiGate, FortiMail, etc.) is removed from FortiAnalyzer. Silently ending log collection from that device — an effective way to make subsequent unauthorized activity on that device invisible to the central store without touching the device's own configuration.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for device/log-source removal events.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system msg="*device*" msg="*remov*"
| table _time, user, devname
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned decommissioning; require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm decommissioning status of the device.
Check whether logging was subsequently disabled or redirected on that device itself (FGT-040).
response_guidance: Re-add the log source immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAnalyzer Log Data Deleted or Purged
description: Log data is manually deleted/purged from FortiAnalyzer storage.
