Since FortiAnalyzer is frequently the longest-retention, most complete copy of Security Fabric telemetry, deliberate log destruction here is treated as Critical anti-forensics activity regardless of how much data was affected.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for manual log-deletion/purge actions.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*log*delet*" OR msg="*log*purg*")
| table _time, user, devname, msg
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate case outside a documented, approved data-retention cleanup — require explicit sign-off for any such action.
investigation_steps: Identify exactly what time range and which devices' logs were purged.
Check for a corresponding compromise indicator elsewhere in the catalogue that this purge may be covering.
response_guidance: Preserve any remaining logs immediately; treat as a confirmed anti-forensics incident pending explicit authorization evidence.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAnalyzer Log Retention Policy Weakened
description: Log retention period or storage allocation is reduced. A softer, slower-acting version of FAZ-005 — rather than deleting logs outright, an attacker (or a poorly-reviewed change) can cause historical evidence to age out faster than intended.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for retention-policy or disk-quota configuration changes reducing the effective retention window.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*retention*" OR msg="*disk*quota*")
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned storage capacity management; require a change ticket and confirm compliance retention minimums are still met.
investigation_steps: Verify the new retention period against compliance/legal requirements.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if it drops below the organization's required minimum retention.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAnalyzer Log Forwarding Destination Changed
description: A log-forwarding destination (to a downstream SIEM, syslog server, or another FortiAnalyzer) is added, removed, or changed. Adding a new destination could quietly copy the organization's full security telemetry stream to an attacker-controlled collector; removing one severs an existing downstream detection pipeline (e.g. this very Splunk integration).
detection_logic: Filters system event log for log-forwarding configuration changes.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system msg="*forward*"
| table _time, user, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned SIEM migration; require a change ticket and validate the new destination is known/owned infrastructure.
investigation_steps: Verify the new destination IP/hostname belongs to organization-owned infrastructure.
Confirm this Splunk pipeline itself was not the one removed.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAnalyzer Alert, Event Handler, or IOC Rule Changed
description: An alert rule, event handler, IOC (indicator-of-compromise) database entry, or automation trigger is disabled or modified within FortiAnalyzer's own detection tooling. Directly analogous to a SOC analyst quietly muting the SIEM's own detection content — the FortiAnalyzer equivalent of disabling auditd or Splunk correlation searches.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for event-handler/alert/IOC configuration changes to a disabled or removed state.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*event handler*" OR msg="*alert*" OR msg="*IOC*") (msg="*disab*" OR msg="*delet*")
| table _time, user, cfgobj, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during content tuning to reduce noise — require a change ticket and a documented reason for disabling rather than tuning a rule.
investigation_steps: Identify which detection content was disabled and why.
Check whether the disabling correlates with an unusual admin login (FAZ-002).
response_guidance: Re-enable unless explicitly justified; treat unexplained disabling as a defense-evasion indicator.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAnalyzer Report Configuration or Automation Stitch Changed
description: A scheduled report definition or automation stitch (action triggered on a detected event, e.g. auto-block via FortiGate API) is modified or disabled. Lower severity than the detection-content changes above, but relevant when the modified automation was itself a security-response mechanism.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for report and automation-stitch configuration changes.
spl:
index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*report*" OR msg="*stitch*") (msg="*modif*" OR msg="*disab*")
| table _time, user, cfgobj, msg
tuning_guidance: High-frequency, mostly benign — prioritize alerting on stitches specifically tagged as security-response automations.
investigation_steps: Determine whether the modified stitch was a security-response automation vs. a routine report.
response_guidance: Restore security-response automations if disabled without authorization.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator User Authentication Failures / Password Spray
description: A single source generates authentication failures against many distinct usernames on FortiAuthenticator, the identity broker frequently sitting in front of FortiGate VPN and admin logins. Compromising authentication here has a multiplier effect across every downstream Fortinet product that relies on it.
detection_logic: Counts distinct usernames attempted per source IP in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_auth status="failed"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(user) as distinct_users, values(user) as usernames_tried, count by srcip, _time
| where distinct_users>=6
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference with any RADIUS clients (FortiGates) that proxy authentication — a single misconfigured client can generate false volume.
investigation_steps: Validate usernames_tried against the real user directory.
Check for any success from the same source.
response_guidance: Block the source at the network layer; force credential rotation for any targeted valid accounts.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator OTP / FortiToken Repeated Failures
description: Repeated failed one-time-password/FortiToken verification attempts for a single user — either a user struggling with a legitimate token, or an attacker who has already obtained the first authentication factor (password) and is now attempting to guess or replay the second factor.
detection_logic: Counts failed OTP verification events per user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_auth auth_type="otp" status="failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count by user, srcip, _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive rate — legitimate users rarely fail OTP verification more than 2-3 times.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user directly whether they were attempting to authenticate.
Check whether the first-factor password was itself recently subject to a guessing attempt (FAC-001).
response_guidance: Lock the account and require re-enrollment of the token if compromise is suspected.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator MFA Fatigue Pattern (Rapid Repeated Push/OTP Prompts)
description: A user receives an unusually high number of MFA push/OTP prompts in a short window — the signature of an MFA-fatigue attack, where an attacker who already has valid first-factor credentials repeatedly triggers authentication prompts hoping the user will eventually approve one out of frustration or confusion.
detection_logic: Counts MFA challenge-issuance events per user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_auth msg="*push*sent*"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as prompt_count by user, _time
| where prompt_count>=5
tuning_guidance: Distinguish from a user simply mistyping a password repeatedly (which triggers FAC-002, not necessarily repeated pushes) — the fatigue pattern is specifically repeated second-factor challenges without a corresponding first-factor failure pattern.
investigation_steps: Contact the user immediately to confirm whether they initiated the prompts.
Check the source IP of the underlying authentication requests generating the prompts.
response_guidance: Force-lock the account and reset credentials immediately; this pattern alone should page the on-call security team given how frequently it precedes real compromise in the wild.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1621: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator Token Reassigned or Removed
description: A FortiToken hardware/mobile token is unassigned from its current user and/or reassigned to a different one. Token reassignment is a direct mechanism for an attacker (or malicious insider) to redirect a victim's second factor to a device they control, effectively taking over MFA for that account without touching the password.
detection_logic: Filters token-management events for reassignment or removal.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event msg="*token*" (msg="*reassign*" OR msg="*remov*" OR msg="*unassign*")
| table _time, admin, user, token_serial, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during device replacement/loss — correlate with a help-desk ticket.
investigation_steps: Confirm the reassignment with the original account owner.
Check for a subsequent VPN/admin login using the reassigned token (FAC-005 correlation).
response_guidance: Reverse unauthorized reassignments immediately and force credential rotation for the affected account.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator Token or Identity Change Followed by VPN Authentication
description: A token reassignment, user creation, or group-membership change on FortiAuthenticator is followed, within a short window, by a successful VPN or administrative authentication using the affected identity. This is the identity-infrastructure-compromise sequence the master specification calls out explicitly — the direct chain from an identity-broker change to its abuse for network access.

data_sources.name: FortiAuthenticator event + authentication log
data_sources.path: identity/token change events; subsequent authentication events
data_sources.description: Identity change correlated with subsequent successful authentication for the same principal.

detection_logic: Correlates a token/identity change event for a given username with a subsequent successful authentication for that same username within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event
| eval stage=case(msg="*token*" AND (msg="*reassign*" OR msg="*creat*"),"1_identity_change", msg="*auth*" AND status="success","2_authenticated", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_identity_change")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, admin, srcip, stage
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for a help-desk-assisted token replacement immediately followed by the user's own next login — cross-reference the change ticket before escalating.
investigation_steps: Verify the identity change against a change/help-desk ticket.
Trace the subsequent VPN session for lateral movement (FGT-058/059).
response_guidance: Disconnect the session and revert the identity change if unconfirmed; treat as a confirmed identity-infrastructure compromise pending verification.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: identity/token change -> successful authentication, same user

title: New FortiAuthenticator User or Group Created
description: A new local user account or group is created within FortiAuthenticator, or an existing user's group membership is modified. Since FortiAuthenticator group membership frequently drives downstream authorization (RADIUS attribute return, VPN group assignment), a group change here can silently grant broader network access without touching the FortiGate at all.

data_sources.name: FortiAuthenticator event log
data_sources.description: User/group creation and membership change events.

detection_logic: Filters identity-management events for user/group creation and membership changes.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event msg="*user*" (msg="*creat*" OR msg="*group*")
| table _time, admin, user, msg
tuning_guidance: Correlate with HR/onboarding for routine new-user creation; focus alerting on group-membership changes affecting privileged groups.
investigation_steps: Verify against onboarding/change records.
Check what network access the new group membership grants downstream.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized accounts/memberships immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator Administrator Account Changes
description: A new FortiAuthenticator administrator is created, or an existing administrator's privilege level is elevated. Compromise of a FortiAuthenticator admin account grants control over the identity broker for the entire Fortinet-authenticated estate.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for administrator account creation/role-change events.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event msg="*admin*" (msg="*creat*" OR msg="*role*" OR msg="*permission*")
| table _time, admin, user, msg
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning — correlate against change management.
investigation_steps: Verify against approved accounts.
Review recent activity by the affected account.
response_guidance: Disable/downgrade immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator LDAP, RADIUS, or SAML Configuration Changed
description: The upstream LDAP directory bind, a RADIUS client's shared secret, or a SAML identity-provider trust relationship is modified. Any of these can be used to redirect authentication trust — a modified SAML IdP/certificate trust in particular can allow an attacker's own identity provider to mint valid-looking assertions for any downstream Fortinet service relying on this SSO trust.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for LDAP/RADIUS/SAML configuration changes.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event (msg="*LDAP*" OR msg="*RADIUS*" OR msg="*SAML*") (msg="*server*" OR msg="*secret*" OR msg="*certificate*" OR msg="*IdP*")
| table _time, admin, cfgobj, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned identity-infrastructure changes; require a change ticket, especially for SAML IdP trust changes.
investigation_steps: Verify the new server/certificate/IdP against known-good infrastructure.
Audit all authentications relying on this trust since the change.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately and audit downstream authorizations granted since the change.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556.004: Network Device Authentication

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator Certificate Changed
description: A trusted CA certificate is added, or the server certificate used for client-certificate/SAML authentication is replaced. A rogue trusted CA addition can let an attacker mint certificates that FortiAuthenticator will accept as valid for certificate-based authentication.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for certificate import/trust-store changes.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event msg="*certificate*" (msg="*import*" OR msg="*trust*")
| table _time, admin, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during certificate renewal cycles; require a change ticket and verify the certificate fingerprint against the expected issuer.
investigation_steps: Verify the certificate's issuing CA and fingerprint.
Check for subsequent certificate-based authentications using the new trust.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized trusted CAs immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1553.004: Install Root Certificate

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiAuthenticator Remote User Sync Configuration Changed
description: The remote-user synchronization configuration (e.g. which upstream directory OU/group is synced, or the sync schedule/source) is changed. Can be used to exclude a legitimate administrator's disablement from propagating, or to include an attacker-controlled directory object into a privileged group unexpectedly.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for remote-sync configuration changes.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event msg="*sync*" (msg="*modif*" OR msg="*creat*")
| table _time, admin, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during directory restructuring; require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Verify the new sync scope against expected directory structure.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiClient EMS Administrator Login Failure / Brute Force
description: Repeated failed administrator login attempts against FortiClient EMS, the console that manages endpoint security policy and isolation status for every enrolled endpoint.
detection_logic: Counts failed EMS admin logins in a rolling window.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event action="login" status="failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, values(srcip) as source_ips by user, _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Minimal legitimate tuning expected.
investigation_steps: Validate targeted usernames.
Check for a subsequent success.
response_guidance: Block the source; treat as management-plane infrastructure.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiClient Endpoint Deregistered or Isolation Removed
description: An endpoint is deregistered from EMS management, or a previously-isolated (quarantined) endpoint has its network isolation removed. Deregistration ends policy enforcement and telemetry entirely; premature de-isolation can return a still-compromised host to full network access before remediation is confirmed complete.
detection_logic: Filters EMS event log for deregistration and isolation-removal events.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event (msg="*deregister*" OR msg="*isolation*removed*")
| table _time, admin, hostname, device_id, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned decommissioning or confirmed remediation; require a change ticket/incident-closure record for de-isolation specifically.
investigation_steps: Confirm decommissioning or remediation-completion records.
For de-isolation, verify the remediation steps were actually completed.
response_guidance: Re-isolate if remediation is not confirmed complete; re-register if deregistration was unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiClient EMS Endpoint Security Policy Weakened
description: An endpoint security profile is modified to disable real-time protection, web filtering, application firewall, or vulnerability scanning components for a policy group. Since EMS policy pushes apply fleet-wide to every endpoint in the affected group, this is the FortiClient equivalent of FMG-015's fleet-wide security control impairment.
detection_logic: Filters EMS event log for security-profile attribute changes to a disabled state, counting affected endpoint group size.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event msg="*policy*" (cfgattr="realtime_protection" OR cfgattr="web_filter" OR cfgattr="vulnerability_scan") msg="*disab*"
| table _time, admin, policy_name, cfgattr
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for performance-sensitive endpoint groups with compensating controls elsewhere — require documented exception per group.
investigation_steps: Identify which endpoint groups the modified policy applies to.
Cross-reference with FortiEDR telemetry for the same hosts if deployed as a compensating layer.
response_guidance: Restore protection settings unless explicitly justified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiClient Telemetry Disconnected or Protection Disabled on Endpoint
description: An endpoint stops reporting telemetry to EMS unexpectedly, or the local FortiClient agent's protection is disabled/uninstalled directly on the endpoint. Either represents a loss of visibility into that specific host — legitimate during maintenance, but also a common local-defense-evasion step once an attacker has interactive access.
detection_logic: Flags endpoints whose last telemetry check-in exceeds an expected heartbeat interval, cross-referenced against known maintenance windows.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen by hostname, device_id
| eval minutes_since=round((now()-last_seen)/60,1)
| where minutes_since>30
tuning_guidance: Exclude hosts undergoing scheduled OS reimaging/patching; requires a maintenance-window lookup to avoid noise.
investigation_steps: Check whether the endpoint is genuinely offline (powered down, network issue) vs. the agent being tampered with locally.
If EDR telemetry is separately available, cross-check whether it also stopped.
response_guidance: Investigate hosts that are network-reachable but not reporting telemetry as a likely local tampering event.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: no telemetry check-in for >30 minutes

title: FortiClient EMS Reports Vulnerability Detected on Endpoint
description: FortiClient's vulnerability scan identifies a known-exploitable software vulnerability on an endpoint. Not an attack in itself, but directly relevant to prioritizing which endpoints are most likely to be successfully exploited if targeted.

data_sources.name: EMS event log
data_sources.description: Detected vulnerabilities with severity and affected software.

detection_logic: Filters vulnerability scan results for high/critical severity findings.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_vuln severity IN ("high","critical")
| table _time, hostname, device_id, cve, software, severity
tuning_guidance: Use as a prioritization input for patch management rather than a standalone SOC alert; high volume expected on unpatched fleets.
investigation_steps: Cross-reference against active exploitation of the specific CVE in threat intelligence.
response_guidance: Prioritize patching; consider isolating the endpoint if the vulnerability is under active exploitation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiClient Malicious Process or Malware Detected
description: FortiClient's local antivirus/anti-malware engine detects and (depending on configuration) blocks a malicious file or process on an endpoint.

data_sources.name: EMS event log
data_sources.description: Local malware detections reported to EMS.

detection_logic: Filters endpoint AV detection events, distinguishing blocked from allowed outcomes.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event msg="*malware*detect*"
| table _time, hostname, device_id, malware_name, action, filepath
tuning_guidance: Escalate specifically when action is not blocked, or when the same malware_name appears across multiple hosts (fleet-wide correlation, see FNT-X-006).
investigation_steps: Confirm the detection was blocked.
Identify the delivery vector (email, web download, removable media).
response_guidance: Isolate the endpoint if the detection was not fully blocked or if follow-on suspicious activity is observed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiClient Web Filter or Application Control Alert on Endpoint
description: The FortiClient local web-filter or application-control component blocks a request on an endpoint operating outside the corporate network perimeter (roaming user), extending the same category of protection covered by FGT-089 through FGT-094 to off-network endpoints.

data_sources.name: EMS event log
data_sources.path: endpoint web filter / app control events
data_sources.description: Local policy enforcement events on roaming endpoints.

detection_logic: Filters endpoint web-filter/app-control events for malicious-category blocks.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event msg="*webfilter*" catdesc IN ("Malicious Websites","Phishing","Command and Control")
| table _time, hostname, device_id, url, catdesc, action
tuning_guidance: Same tuning approach as FGT-092/093 — escalate on repeated blocks from the same endpoint.
investigation_steps: Check whether the endpoint is on or off the corporate network at time of detection.
response_guidance: Escalate per the repeated-blocks pattern (see EMS-008-equivalent reasoning in FGT-093) if the same endpoint repeats.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiClient EMS ZTNA Tag Changed to Grant Broader Access
description: A Zero Trust Network Access posture tag is manually assigned to an endpoint or its evaluation criteria weakened, potentially granting an endpoint access to ZTNA-gated resources despite not actually meeting the intended compliance posture (patch level, AV status, disk encryption, etc.).

data_sources.name: EMS event log
data_sources.description: ZTNA compliance tag rule and assignment changes.

detection_logic: Filters EMS event log for ZTNA tag rule modifications or manual tag overrides.
spl:
index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event msg="*ZTNA*tag*" (msg="*modif*" OR msg="*overrid*" OR msg="*manual*")
| table _time, admin, device_id, tag_name, msg
tuning_guidance: Manual overrides should be rare and time-boxed (e.g. temporary exception during a known compliance gap) — require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Verify the endpoint's actual compliance posture against the assigned tag.
Check what ZTNA-gated resources the tag now grants access to.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized tag overrides; re-evaluate the endpoint's real posture.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1599: Network Boundary Bridging

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Malicious Process Blocked
description: FortiEDR's behavioral engine identifies and blocks a malicious process execution. FortiEDR's post-execution/behavioral detection model catches classes of threats (fileless malware, living-off-the-land abuse) that signature-based FortiClient AV and network-layer FortiGate controls cannot see.

data_sources.name: FortiEDR event log
data_sources.description: Blocked malicious process events with process tree.

detection_logic: Filters FortiEDR event log for blocked malicious-classification process events.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event event_type="process" action="blocked" classification="malicious"
| table _time, hostname, process_name, process_path, parent_process, classification
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive rate given the malicious-classification filter; investigate every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Review the full process tree/parent chain.
Check for related network activity from the host around the same time (correlate with FortiGate traffic logs).
response_guidance: Confirm the block was effective; if any related process was NOT blocked, isolate the host immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Suspicious Process Tree or Living-off-the-Land Binary Abuse
description: A legitimate, dual-use system binary (PowerShell, cmd.exe, wmic, mshta, rundll32, certutil, and similar LOLBins) is spawned by an unusual parent process or with suspicious command-line arguments — the process-tree-based detection style specific to EDR platforms and impossible to derive from network logs alone.

data_sources.name: FortiEDR event log
data_sources.description: Process creation events with parent/child relationship and command line.

detection_logic: Filters process-creation events for known LOLBin process names spawned by an unexpected parent (e.g. an Office application, browser, or script host rather than explorer.exe/a management tool).
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event event_type="process"
| where match(process_name, "(?i)(powershell|cmd\.exe|wmic|mshta|rundll32|certutil)")
| lookup fedr_expected_parents.csv process_name parent_process OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, hostname, process_name, parent_process, command_line
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained expected-parent lookup tuned to your environment's legitimate automation/scripting patterns — high false-positive rate without it.
investigation_steps: Review the full command line for obfuscation/encoding.
Trace the process tree back to the ultimate root cause (e.g. an Office macro, browser download).
response_guidance: Isolate the host and investigate as a likely active intrusion.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter
MITRE ATT&CK T1218: System Binary Proxy Execution

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Credential Dumping / LSASS Memory Access Blocked
description: FortiEDR detects and blocks an attempt to access LSASS process memory — the primary mechanism tools like Mimikatz use to extract plaintext credentials, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos tickets from a live Windows host.

data_sources.name: FortiEDR event log
data_sources.description: LSASS memory access attempts by process.

detection_logic: Filters memory-access events where target_process is lsass.exe.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event event_type="memory_access" target_process="lsass.exe"
| table _time, hostname, process_name, process_path, action
tuning_guidance: Legitimate security tooling (some EDR/AV engines themselves, certain backup/credential-vault agents) may access LSASS — maintain an allowlist of known-legitimate accessors.
investigation_steps: Confirm the accessing process is not a known legitimate tool.
Treat as a credential-theft attempt and assume any credentials cached in memory on this host are compromised.
response_guidance: Isolate the host immediately; force domain-wide credential rotation for any account that had an active session on this host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Ransomware Behavior Detected
description: FortiEDR's behavioral ransomware protection identifies mass file-modification/encryption activity consistent with ransomware — typically a process rapidly reading, encrypting, and rewriting many files with new extensions across the filesystem in a short window.

data_sources.name: FortiEDR event log
data_sources.description: Mass file modification detection with process attribution.

detection_logic: Filters FortiEDR event log for ransomware-classification behavioral detections.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event classification="ransomware"
| table _time, hostname, process_name, process_path, files_affected, action
tuning_guidance: Extremely low tolerable false-positive rate given the impact of a true positive — validate against any legitimate high-volume file-encryption software (backup/archival tools) in your environment ahead of time via an allowlist.
investigation_steps: Confirm the process was actually blocked/killed.
Assess blast radius: check whether the process reached network shares before being stopped.
response_guidance: Isolate the host immediately regardless of block status; this should trigger the organization's ransomware incident response plan without delay.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Persistence Mechanism Established
description: FortiEDR identifies a process creating a persistence mechanism — a registry Run key, scheduled task, startup-folder entry, or new service — associated with a process already flagged as suspicious or unsigned.

data_sources.name: FortiEDR event log
data_sources.description: Registry/scheduled-task/service creation events attributed to a process.

detection_logic: Filters FortiEDR event log for persistence-classification events.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event classification="persistence"
| table _time, hostname, process_name, process_path, persistence_type, target, action
tuning_guidance: Exclude known legitimate software-installer processes that create scheduled tasks/services as part of normal installation — maintain a signed-vendor allowlist.
investigation_steps: Verify the creating process's signature/reputation.
Check what the persistence mechanism launches on trigger.
response_guidance: Remove the persistence mechanism and isolate the host if the creating process is confirmed malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1547.001: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Process Injection or Process Hollowing Detected
description: FortiEDR identifies memory manipulation consistent with process injection or process hollowing — a technique used to run malicious code within the memory space of a legitimate, trusted process to evade both signature-based and some behavioral detection.
detection_logic: Filters FortiEDR event log for process-injection-classification events.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event classification="process_injection"
| table _time, hostname, source_process, target_process, action
tuning_guidance: Very low legitimate-use rate; some application virtualization or DRM software can trigger false positives — allowlist by verified vendor signature.
investigation_steps: Identify both the source (injecting) and target (injected-into) processes.
Treat the target process as compromised even though it is normally legitimate.
response_guidance: Isolate the host immediately and treat as an active, sophisticated intrusion.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Suspicious Driver Loaded
description: An unsigned or unusual kernel driver is loaded on an endpoint. Kernel-mode code execution is one of the highest-privilege footholds available on a Windows host and is frequently used by advanced malware/rootkits and by BYOVD ("bring your own vulnerable driver") attacks that abuse a legitimately-signed-but-vulnerable driver to gain kernel access.

data_sources.name: FortiEDR event log
data_sources.description: Kernel driver load events with signature status.

detection_logic: Filters driver-load events where signed=false or the driver is on a known-vulnerable-driver watchlist.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event event_type="driver_load"
| lookup fedr_vulnerable_drivers.csv driver_name OUTPUT is_known_vulnerable
| where signed="false" OR is_known_vulnerable="true"
| table _time, hostname, driver_name, signed, is_known_vulnerable, action
tuning_guidance: Maintain the known-vulnerable-driver watchlist from current LOLDrivers-style community references; unsigned-driver-only filtering alone will miss BYOVD attacks using legitimately-signed drivers.
investigation_steps: Identify the driver's origin and loading process.
Treat kernel-level compromise as the working assumption pending investigation.
response_guidance: Isolate the host immediately; kernel-level compromise may require a full rebuild rather than remediation in place.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1547: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Network C2 Communication Blocked
description: FortiEDR's network module identifies and blocks a process attempting outbound communication classified as command-and-control — endpoint-side network detection that operates even for traffic never traversing a FortiGate-inspected network path (e.g. on a roaming laptop off the corporate network).

data_sources.name: FortiEDR event log
data_sources.description: Process-attributed network connections classified as C2.

detection_logic: Filters FortiEDR network-event log for C2-classification events.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event event_type="network" classification="c2"
| table _time, hostname, process_name, dest_ip, dest_port, action
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive rate given the C2 classification; investigate every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Identify the responsible process and its full execution history on the host.
Cross-reference the destination against FortiGate traffic logs if the host was on the corporate network at any point (FNT-X-005).
response_guidance: Isolate the host; treat as a confirmed active C2 channel.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Detects Lateral Movement Tooling
description: FortiEDR identifies process/network behavior consistent with lateral movement tooling — remote service creation, WMI-based remote execution, or PsExec-style admin-share abuse originating from the endpoint.
detection_logic: Filters FortiEDR event log for lateral-movement-classification events.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event classification="lateral_movement"
| table _time, hostname, process_name, target_host, action
tuning_guidance: Allowlist known IT administration tooling (RMM agents, patch management) that legitimately performs remote execution.
investigation_steps: Identify every target_host touched.
Correlate with FortiGate internal traffic (FGT-059) for the same source/destination pair.
response_guidance: Isolate the source host and investigate all target hosts for follow-on compromise.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.002: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
MITRE ATT&CK T1021.006: Windows Remote Management

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiEDR Prevention Policy Disabled or Set to Simulation Mode
description: A FortiEDR prevention policy is switched from blocking mode to simulation/detect-only mode, or disabled outright, for one or more endpoint groups. This is the endpoint-protection equivalent of FGT-034/041 — it can silently convert a would-have-been-blocked threat into a merely-logged one.
detection_logic: Filters FortiEDR management event log for policy mode changes to simulation/disabled.
spl:
index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event msg="*policy*" (mode="simulation" OR mode="disabled")
| table _time, admin, policy_name, mode
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during a controlled rollout/testing phase for a new policy — require a change ticket and time-box the exception.
investigation_steps: Identify which endpoint groups are affected.
Check for any subsequent malicious-classification events that would have been blocked under normal policy.
response_guidance: Restore blocking mode immediately unless explicitly authorized and time-boxed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb SQL Injection Attempt Blocked
description: FortiWeb's signature engine identifies and blocks a SQL injection attempt against a protected web application.

data_sources.name: FortiWeb attack log
data_sources.description: SQL injection signature matches with source, target URL, and action.

detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for SQL injection signature category.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack attack_type="sql_injection"
| table _time, srcip, http_host, http_url, action, severity
tuning_guidance: Tune signature sensitivity against legitimate application query patterns that resemble SQL syntax (e.g. search fields); false positives are common on poorly-tuned WAF profiles.
investigation_steps: Check whether the attempt was blocked.
Review for repeated attempts from the same source (FWB-009).
response_guidance: No emergency action for a blocked attempt; escalate immediately for any allowed hit.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Attempt Blocked
description: FortiWeb identifies and blocks a cross-site scripting attempt in a request parameter, header, or body.
detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for the XSS signature category.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack attack_type="cross_site_scripting"
| table _time, srcip, http_host, http_url, action
tuning_guidance: Common false-positive source: legitimate applications passing HTML/script-like content through rich-text fields — maintain per-application exceptions.
investigation_steps: Check whether the attempt was blocked and whether it targeted an authenticated session (potential stored-XSS follow-up).
response_guidance: No action for blocked attempts; investigate allowed hits for successful script execution.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Command Injection or OS Command Execution Attempt
description: FortiWeb identifies a request attempting to inject OS-level commands into the backend application — one of the highest-impact web attack classes since successful exploitation typically grants direct code execution on the application server.
detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for the command injection signature category.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack attack_type="command_injection"
| table _time, srcip, http_host, http_url, action, http_method
tuning_guidance: Low legitimate false-positive rate for this signature class — investigate every occurrence regardless of block status.
investigation_steps: Confirm the attempt was blocked.
If allowed, immediately investigate the backend application server for signs of command execution.
response_guidance: Treat any allowed hit as a likely successful compromise of the backend server; isolate it pending investigation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application
MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Path Traversal or Local/Remote File Inclusion Attempt
description: FortiWeb identifies a request attempting directory traversal or file inclusion (LFI/RFI) — patterns like `../../etc/passwd` or a parameter pointing at a remote attacker-hosted file — used to read sensitive files or achieve code execution via an included malicious file.

data_sources.name: FortiWeb attack log
data_sources.description: Path traversal / file inclusion signature matches.

detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for path traversal and file inclusion categories.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack (attack_type="path_traversal" OR attack_type="file_inclusion")
| table _time, srcip, http_host, http_url, action
tuning_guidance: Low legitimate false-positive rate.
investigation_steps: Check whether the traversal pattern targeted a sensitive file (config, credentials).
Investigate allowed hits on the backend filesystem.
response_guidance: Investigate any allowed hit immediately for evidence of file disclosure or code execution via inclusion.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Attempt
description: FortiWeb identifies a request attempting to make the backend server issue requests to an attacker-chosen destination — commonly used to reach internal-only services (cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin panels) that are not directly Internet-reachable, making SSRF a frequent stepping stone to internal reconnaissance or credential theft in cloud environments.
detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for the SSRF signature category.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack attack_type="ssrf"
| table _time, srcip, http_host, http_url, action
tuning_guidance: Applications that legitimately fetch user-supplied URLs (webhooks, link previews) are the main false-positive source — maintain per-application exceptions with strict destination allowlisting instead of disabling the signature.
investigation_steps: Identify the target destination the request attempted to reach.
If the target is a cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254), treat as high priority regardless of block status.
response_guidance: Investigate any allowed hit for credential exposure via cloud metadata service abuse.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb XML External Entity (XXE) or Insecure Deserialization Attempt
description: FortiWeb identifies a request containing an XXE payload (malicious XML external entity declaration) or a serialized-object payload consistent with insecure deserialization — both attack classes that can lead to file disclosure, SSRF, or remote code execution depending on the backend framework.
detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for XXE and deserialization categories.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack (attack_type="xxe" OR attack_type="deserialization")
| table _time, srcip, http_host, http_url, action
tuning_guidance: Low legitimate false-positive rate for well-formed XXE signatures; deserialization detection is more framework-specific and may need per-application tuning.
investigation_steps: Identify the targeted application/framework.
Investigate allowed hits for backend impact.
response_guidance: Investigate any allowed hit immediately; these attack classes frequently lead directly to remote code execution.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Web Shell Upload or Detection
description: FortiWeb identifies a file upload matching a known web-shell pattern, or an existing web shell being accessed on the protected application. A web shell represents established persistent remote code execution on the application server and should be treated as the highest-priority WAF finding available.
detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for web-shell-classification events.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack attack_type="webshell"
| table _time, srcip, http_host, http_url, filename, action
tuning_guidance: Very low legitimate false-positive rate — investigate every occurrence with urgency regardless of blocked/allowed status.
investigation_steps: Confirm the upload was blocked; if not, immediately search the web root for the uploaded file.
Review all subsequent requests to the same URL path.
response_guidance: If the upload succeeded, treat the application server as compromised: remove the shell, isolate the server, and conduct a full forensic review of the application.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Credential Stuffing / Brute Force Against Application Login
description: FortiWeb's brute-force/credential-stuffing protection identifies a high rate of login attempts against a protected application's authentication endpoint, consistent with automated credential-stuffing tooling testing breached username/password pairs.

data_sources.name: FortiWeb attack log
data_sources.description: Login attempt rate against protected authentication endpoints.

detection_logic: Filters FortiWeb attack log for brute-force/credential-stuffing classification.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack attack_type="brute_force"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, dc(http_url) as distinct_endpoints by srcip, http_host, _time
| where count>=20
tuning_guidance: Exclude known load-testing or QA automation source IPs.
investigation_steps: Check for a successful login among the attempts.
Review the application's own authentication logs if available outside FortiWeb.
response_guidance: Block the source; enforce/verify MFA on the targeted application if not already required.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Repeated Exploit Attempts From Same Source (Scanner Activity)
description: A single source IP triggers many distinct WAF signature categories against one or more protected applications in a short window — consistent with an automated vulnerability scanner or exploit framework running a broad attack-pattern sweep rather than a single targeted attempt.
detection_logic: Counts distinct attack_type categories triggered per source IP in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack
| bin _time span=10m
| stats dc(attack_type) as distinct_categories, count, values(attack_type) as categories by srcip, _time
| where distinct_categories>=5 OR count>=30
tuning_guidance: Exclude authorized vulnerability scanning/pentest source ranges during scheduled assessment windows.
investigation_steps: Review categories to identify the scanner's focus.
Check for any allowed hits among the many attempts.
response_guidance: Block the source IP; verify no attempts succeeded.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb API Abuse: Excessive Requests or Parameter Fuzzing Against API Endpoint
description: A source generates an unusually high request rate or high parameter-value diversity against a single API endpoint — consistent with automated API fuzzing/enumeration (e.g. testing sequential object IDs for an IDOR vulnerability, or a credential-stuffing bot targeting an API rather than the web login form).

data_sources.name: FortiWeb API protection log
data_sources.description: Per-endpoint request rate and parameter patterns.

detection_logic: Counts requests per (srcip, http_url) pair in a rolling window and flags high-volume outliers.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_api
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count by srcip, http_url, _time
| where count>=100
tuning_guidance: Exclude known high-volume legitimate API consumers (mobile app backends, partner integrations) via an allowlist keyed on API key/client ID rather than source IP alone.
investigation_steps: Identify the API client (key/token) responsible.
Check for a data-access pattern consistent with IDOR enumeration (sequential IDs returning varied user data).
response_guidance: Rate-limit or block the offending client; review the endpoint for authorization (IDOR) vulnerabilities.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Bot / Automated Scraper Activity Detected
description: FortiWeb's bot-detection engine (behavioral/biometric analysis, known-bot signature, or CAPTCHA-failure pattern) flags automated non-human traffic against a protected application — commonly content scraping, price/inventory harvesting, or reconnaissance ahead of a more targeted attack.

data_sources.name: FortiWeb bot mitigation log
data_sources.description: Bot classification events by source and confidence.

detection_logic: Filters bot mitigation log for high-confidence bot classifications.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_bot bot_confidence="high"
| table _time, srcip, http_host, action
tuning_guidance: Exclude known legitimate crawlers (search engine bots) via a verified-bot allowlist.
investigation_steps: Assess business impact (content scraping vs. reconnaissance for a more targeted follow-up).
response_guidance: Apply rate-limiting/CAPTCHA challenge if not already active; escalate if bot activity correlates with subsequent exploit attempts from related sources.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1596: Search Open Technical Databases

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb WAF Policy Weakened or Signature Set Disabled
description: A FortiWeb protection profile is changed from block to monitor-only mode, or a signature category (e.g. SQL injection, XSS) is disabled entirely. Since FortiWeb frequently protects the organization's most business-critical Internet-facing applications, this is a critical-severity change regardless of which specific category was affected.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events for protection profile action-mode changes to monitor/alert-only, or signature category disablement.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_event type=event subtype=system msg="*profile*" (msg="*monitor*" OR msg="*disab*")
| table _time, admin, profile_name, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during a controlled tuning phase for a new signature category — require a change ticket and time-box the exception.
investigation_steps: Identify which application(s) and signature categories are affected.
Check for any attack attempts against the now-weakened protection since the change.
response_guidance: Restore blocking mode immediately unless explicitly authorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb WAF Exploit Attempt Followed by Outbound Connection From Backend Server
description: A WAF exploit signature match against a protected application is followed, within a short window, by the backend application server making an unusual outbound connection — chaining a web-layer attack to its likely next stage in the same way FGT-083 chains an IPS hit to outbound C2.

data_sources.name: FortiWeb attack log + FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: WAF exploit hit against a known application server IP, correlated with that server's own subsequent outbound connections.

detection_logic: Correlates a WAF exploit event where the protected application's backend IP is known, with a subsequent outbound connection from that same backend IP to a new/rare destination.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack severity="critical"
| lookup fwb_backend_ips.csv http_host OUTPUT backend_ip
| eval victim=backend_ip, stage="1_exploited"
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound"
  | lookup fgt_dest_baseline.csv srcip dstip OUTPUT is_known
  | where isnull(is_known)
  | eval victim=srcip, stage="2_new_outbound" ]
| transaction victim maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_exploited")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, victim, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained mapping of protected application hostnames to their real backend server IPs, and a per-host destination baseline — validate both data sources before enabling as a paging alert.
investigation_steps: Treat as a likely successful application-server compromise.
Isolate the backend server pending investigation.
response_guidance: Isolate the backend server, block the outbound destination, and initiate incident response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: WAF exploit hit -> new/rare outbound connection from backend server

title: FortiMail Phishing Email Detected
description: FortiMail's anti-phishing engine classifies an inbound message as phishing. The baseline detection for the FortiMail section — most of the higher-severity detections below refine or correlate on top of this class of event.
detection_logic: Filters FortiMail history log for phishing-disposition messages.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history disposition="phishing"
| table _time, from, to, subject, action
tuning_guidance: Expected background rate; escalate specifically on delivered (not quarantined) phishing or repeated targeting of the same recipient (FML-002).
investigation_steps: Confirm the message was quarantined/blocked rather than delivered.
response_guidance: No emergency action for a blocked message; investigate any delivered phishing message with the recipient directly.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Phishing or Malware Email Delivered (Not Blocked)
description: A message classified as phishing or containing malware is delivered to the recipient's inbox rather than quarantined or blocked — meaning the intended victim has direct access to the malicious content, and user-execution-dependent compromise (a click, an attachment open) is now only one action away.

data_sources.name: FortiMail log
data_sources.description: Malicious message classification with delivery outcome.

detection_logic: Filters FortiMail history log for malicious-classification messages where action indicates delivery rather than quarantine/reject.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history (disposition="phishing" OR disposition="malware") action="delivered"
| table _time, from, to, subject, disposition
tuning_guidance: Every occurrence warrants review — this combination should be rare if anti-phishing/anti-malware profiles are well-tuned.
investigation_steps: Contact the recipient immediately to confirm whether the message was opened/clicked.
Retract/quarantine the message from the mailbox if the mail platform supports it.
response_guidance: Retract the message if possible, alert the recipient, and monitor their account/endpoint for follow-on compromise indicators.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Malicious Attachment Detected
description: An inbound message attachment is identified as malware by FortiMail's antivirus/sandbox integration.
detection_logic: Filters FortiMail history log for malware-disposition messages.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history disposition="malware"
| table _time, from, to, subject, attachment_name, virus_name, action
tuning_guidance: Escalate on repeated attachments with the same hash/virus_name across multiple recipients (mass campaign, see FML-011) or any delivered instance (FML-002).
investigation_steps: Check FortiSandbox verdict detail if the attachment was submitted for sandboxing (FSB-### detections).
response_guidance: No emergency action for a blocked attachment; investigate delivered instances per FML-002.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Malicious URL in Message Body
description: A URL embedded in an inbound message body matches FortiGuard's malicious/phishing URL category. Distinct from the general phishing disposition since URL-based attacks specifically rely on the recipient clicking through rather than opening an attachment.

data_sources.name: FortiMail log
data_sources.path: history log with URL scan results

detection_logic: Filters FortiMail history log for messages containing a URL flagged as malicious/phishing category.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history msg="*URL*" catdesc IN ("Malicious Websites","Phishing")
| table _time, from, to, subject, url, action
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference click-through data if FortiMail's URL click-protection/rewrite feature is enabled — a recorded click is a much higher-priority finding than the message alone.
investigation_steps: Check whether the URL-rewrite/click-protection feature recorded an actual click.
response_guidance: If a click was recorded, treat as a likely credential-phishing success and force a password reset for the targeted account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Domain or Display-Name Spoofing Detected
description: An inbound message fails SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment for its claimed sending domain, or its display name impersonates a known internal executive/domain while the underlying envelope-from address does not match — the core signature of both domain spoofing and Business Email Compromise (BEC) impersonation attempts.

data_sources.name: FortiMail log
data_sources.description: Authentication alignment results and display-name impersonation checks.

detection_logic: Filters FortiMail history log for messages failing DMARC alignment or matching a display-name-impersonation policy for protected executive names.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history (dmarc_result="fail" OR (spf_result="fail" AND dkim_result="fail"))
| lookup fml_protected_names.csv display_name OUTPUT is_protected_name
| table _time, from, to, display_name, spf_result, dkim_result, dmarc_result, is_protected_name
tuning_guidance: Maintain the protected-executive-name list; DMARC-fail-only filtering without display-name correlation will be noisy against legitimate mailing lists and forwarders that break alignment benignly.
investigation_steps: Prioritize investigation on messages matching a protected display name.
Check for a financial or credential-related request in the message body (classic BEC pattern).
response_guidance: Quarantine and alert the impersonated individual and the targeted recipient; treat protected-name matches as high priority regardless of DMARC status.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Business Email Compromise (BEC) Pattern Detected
description: A message combines domain/display-name spoofing (FML-005) with content patterns characteristic of Business Email Compromise — urgency language, a request to change payment/banking details, a wire-transfer request, or a request to purchase gift cards, particularly when purporting to be from an executive.

data_sources.name: FortiMail log
data_sources.description: BEC-pattern content classification combined with spoofing indicators.

detection_logic: Combines FML-005's spoofing signal with FortiMail's own BEC/impersonation content classifier (or a keyword-based fallback for wire-transfer/gift-card/urgency language).
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history
| lookup fml_protected_names.csv display_name OUTPUT is_protected_name
| where is_protected_name="true" AND match(subject."\n".msg, "(?i)(wire transfer|urgent|gift card|payment details|banking information|confidential)")
| table _time, from, to, subject, display_name
tuning_guidance: Content-keyword matching is inherently imprecise — treat this as a triage/hunting search rather than a precision alert, and prioritize by is_protected_name matches specifically.
investigation_steps: Contact the impersonated executive and the recipient directly and immediately — do not rely on email to verify.
Check whether any funds were transferred or gift cards purchased before detection.
response_guidance: If funds were transferred, engage the bank/payment processor for a recall attempt immediately; this is a time-critical response scenario.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Anomalous Outbound Email Volume From Single Account
description: A single mailbox sends an unusually high volume of outbound messages compared to its own baseline — the classic signature of a compromised mailbox being used to send further phishing/spam, either to the organization's contact list or externally.
detection_logic: Counts outbound messages per sender in a rolling window and flags counts far above that sender's historical baseline.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history direction="outbound"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as msg_count, dc(to) as distinct_recipients by from, _time
| eventstats avg(msg_count) as avg_count, stdev(msg_count) as stdev_count by from
| eval zscore=round((msg_count-avg_count)/(stdev_count+1),2)
| where zscore>=3 AND msg_count>=50
tuning_guidance: Exclude known bulk-mail/marketing service accounts; this detection is specifically for individual mailboxes that don't normally send high volume.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the account owner whether they sent this volume of email.
Review recipient list for signs of an address-book-harvesting spam campaign.
response_guidance: Lock the account and force a password reset if unconfirmed; treat as a confirmed compromise pending verification.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: z-score >= 3, minimum 50 messages/hour

title: FortiMail Outbound Email Contains Sensitive Data Pattern (DLP)
description: FortiMail's DLP engine identifies an outbound message containing a pattern matching sensitive data classes (SSNs, credit card numbers, or organization-specific confidential markers) sent to an external recipient.

data_sources.name: FortiMail DLP log
data_sources.description: Sensitive-data pattern matches on outbound mail.

detection_logic: Filters FortiMail DLP log for outbound matches to external recipients.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_dlp direction="outbound" recipient_domain!="*yourdomain.com*"
| table _time, from, to, dlp_rule, action
tuning_guidance: Tune DLP rule patterns against known false-positive sources (test data, legitimately-shared reports with an approved external partner allowlist).
investigation_steps: Confirm with the sender whether the transfer was authorized.
Identify what specific data pattern triggered the DLP match.
response_guidance: Block if unauthorized; escalate to data-protection/privacy team for any confirmed regulated-data exposure.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1567: Exfiltration Over Web Service
MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Administrator Changes
description: A new FortiMail administrator is created, or an existing administrator's privilege level is elevated. FortiMail administrators can access message quarantine content, adjust filtering policy, and release/redirect mail — a compromised admin account can both expose sensitive email content and weaken the organization's phishing/malware defenses fleet-wide.
detection_logic: Filters system event log for administrator creation/role-change events.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_event type=event subtype=system msg="*admin*" (msg="*creat*" OR msg="*role*")
| table _time, admin, user, msg
tuning_guidance: No routine tuning — correlate against change management.
investigation_steps: Verify against approved accounts.
Review recent quarantine-release and policy-change activity by the account.
response_guidance: Disable/downgrade immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Antispam/Antiphishing Policy Weakened or Allowlist Entry Added
description: A sender/domain allowlist entry is added, or the antispam/antiphishing action for a policy is weakened from quarantine/reject to accept. A domain added to the allowlist bypasses all downstream filtering entirely, making it a favored technique for whitelisting an attacker-controlled sending domain in advance of a phishing campaign.

data_sources.name: FortiMail event log
data_sources.description: Allowlist and policy action configuration changes.

detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events for allowlist additions and policy action weakening.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_event type=event subtype=system (msg="*safelist*" OR msg="*allow*list*" OR (msg="*policy*" AND msg="*action*"))
| table _time, admin, cfgobj, msg
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for known-good partner domains; require a change ticket and periodic review of the allowlist for stale/suspicious entries.
investigation_steps: Verify the added domain/sender against a known business relationship.
Check for a subsequent phishing campaign from the newly-allowlisted sender.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized allowlist entries immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiMail Quarantine Release Anomaly
description: A message is released from quarantine by an administrator (rather than the intended recipient via self-service release) for a message classified as malware or high-confidence phishing, or an unusual volume of releases occurs in a short window.

data_sources.name: FortiMail log
data_sources.description: Quarantine release actions with releaser identity.

detection_logic: Filters quarantine-release events where the original disposition was malware/high-confidence phishing and the releaser is an administrator account.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_quarantine action="released" (disposition="malware" OR disposition="phishing")
| table _time, admin, from, to, disposition
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for confirmed false-positive releases after review — require the releasing administrator to document the justification.
investigation_steps: Confirm the release was a deliberate, reviewed false-positive correction.
If not, treat as a potential insider-assisted or compromised-admin phishing delivery.
response_guidance: Re-quarantine if unconfirmed and investigate the releasing account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiProxy Malicious URL or Malware Download Blocked
description: FortiProxy's web filter or antivirus engine blocks a request to a malicious URL or a malware file download for an explicit-proxy client. FortiProxy sits as a forward proxy for outbound web traffic, giving it visibility into user-initiated downloads that a purely transparent inline deployment (FortiGate) might see differently depending on architecture.

data_sources.name: FortiProxy traffic/security log
data_sources.path: proxy access log with security verdict

detection_logic: Filters FortiProxy log for malicious-category or malware-verdict blocked requests.
spl:
index=fortiproxy sourcetype=fpx_traffic (catdesc="Malicious Websites" OR catdesc="Command and Control" OR virus_name!="")
| table _time, srcip, user, url, catdesc, virus_name, action
tuning_guidance: Same tuning approach as the equivalent FortiGate web-filter/antivirus detections (FGT-085/092).
investigation_steps: Confirm the request was blocked.
Identify the source user/host.
response_guidance: No emergency action for a blocked request; investigate any allowed hit.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiProxy Outbound Connection to C2 or Anonymizer Category
description: A proxied client connects to a destination categorized as command-and-control or an anonymization/proxy service — the FortiProxy equivalent of FGT-075, relevant specifically for organizations that route egress traffic through FortiProxy rather than (or in addition to) FortiGate.
detection_logic: Filters FortiProxy log for the Command and Control and Proxy/Anonymizer categories.
spl:
index=fortiproxy sourcetype=fpx_traffic (catdesc="Command and Control" OR catdesc="Proxy and Anonymizer")
| table _time, srcip, user, url, action
tuning_guidance: Requires an up-to-date FortiGuard category database; low false-positive rate for the C2 category specifically.
investigation_steps: Investigate the source host for malware.
Check whether the connection was blocked.
response_guidance: Investigate and remediate the source host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiProxy Unusual Upload Volume Through Proxy
description: A proxied client uploads an unusually large volume of data through the proxy in a rolling window — the FortiProxy equivalent of FGT-071/097, relevant since proxied uploads are a common exfiltration path from environments that force all outbound traffic through an explicit proxy.

data_sources.name: FortiProxy traffic log
data_sources.path: proxy access log with byte counts

detection_logic: Aggregates uploaded bytes per source host per hour and flags values above that host's historical baseline.
spl:
index=fortiproxy sourcetype=fpx_traffic
| bin _time span=1h
| stats sum(sentbyte) as total_sent by srcip, user, _time
| eventstats avg(total_sent) as avg_sent, stdev(total_sent) as stdev_sent by srcip
| eval zscore=round((total_sent-avg_sent)/(stdev_sent+1),2)
| where zscore>=3 AND total_sent>=200000000
tuning_guidance: Exclude known backup/sync service accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify the destination and user.
Correlate with FGT-070/097 if the same host also traverses FortiGate for other traffic.
response_guidance: Investigate the source host and destination.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: z-score >= 3, minimum 200MB/hour

title: FortiProxy Authentication Attacks
description: Repeated failed proxy authentication attempts for a single user or from a single source — the same brute-force/spray pattern class as FGT-002/003, applied to explicit-proxy authentication credentials.
detection_logic: Counts failed proxy authentication attempts per user/source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortiproxy sourcetype=fpx_auth status="failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, dc(user) as distinct_users by srcip, _time
| where count>=5 OR distinct_users>=6
tuning_guidance: Exclude any application/service that legitimately re-authenticates frequently against the proxy.
investigation_steps: Validate targeted usernames.
Check for a subsequent success.
response_guidance: Block the source; investigate the targeted account(s).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiProxy SSL Inspection Bypass or Category Override Added
description: SSL inspection is disabled or a category/destination exemption is added on FortiProxy — the FortiProxy equivalent of FGT-095, with the same visibility-loss consequences for proxied traffic.
detection_logic: Filters configuration-change events for SSL inspection profile downgrades or new exemptions.
spl:
index=fortiproxy sourcetype=fpx_event type=event subtype=system cfgpath="firewall.ssl-ssh-profile"
| table _time, admin, cfgobj, cfgattr, action
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for certificate-pinned applications; maintain a reviewed exemption list.
investigation_steps: Identify scope and justification of the change.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiProxy Outbound Tunneling Application Detected
description: A proxied client's traffic pattern matches a known tunneling technique (CONNECT-method abuse to non-standard ports, WebSocket-based tunneling tools) — used to smuggle non-HTTP protocols through an HTTP(S) proxy.
detection_logic: Filters proxy CONNECT-method requests to ports outside the standard 443/8443 range.
spl:
index=fortiproxy sourcetype=fpx_traffic method="CONNECT"
| where dstport!=443 AND dstport!=8443
| table _time, srcip, user, dstip, dstport
tuning_guidance: Exclude known legitimate applications that use CONNECT to non-standard ports (some collaboration/VoIP tools).
investigation_steps: Identify the destination and application responsible.
response_guidance: Investigate and block if no legitimate purpose is identified.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiSandbox Malicious File Verdict
description: FortiSandbox's dynamic analysis engine returns a malicious verdict for a submitted file (from FortiGate, FortiMail, FortiWeb, or manual submission). Because sandbox verdicts arrive after the file has already been forwarded for delivery/execution in many deployment modes, a malicious verdict here often means the source system needs to act retroactively.

data_sources.name: FortiSandbox verdict log
data_sources.description: File analysis job submissions and verdicts.

detection_logic: Filters FortiSandbox verdict log for malicious-classification results.
spl:
index=fortisandbox sourcetype=fsb_verdict verdict="malicious"
| table _time, filename, file_hash, source_product, submitting_device
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive rate; investigate every malicious verdict, prioritizing files that were already delivered before the verdict returned (check source_product's own delivery-status field).
investigation_steps: Check whether the source product (FortiGate/FortiMail/FortiWeb) already delivered the file before the verdict returned.
Search for the same file_hash across other endpoints/mail recipients (FML-003/FGT-087/FNT-X-009).
response_guidance: If the file was already delivered, treat the recipient host/mailbox as compromised and investigate immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiSandbox High-Risk / Suspicious Document Verdict
description: A submitted document (Office file, PDF) returns a high-risk/suspicious (not outright malicious) verdict — typically indicating macro-based or script-based behavior consistent with a dropper or downloader that the sandbox could not fully confirm as malicious within its analysis window.
detection_logic: Filters FortiSandbox verdict log for suspicious/high-risk classification on document file types.
spl:
index=fortisandbox sourcetype=fsb_verdict verdict="suspicious" file_type IN ("doc","docx","xls","xlsx","pdf")
| table _time, filename, file_hash, risk_score, submitting_device
tuning_guidance: Track risk_score trends; a suspicious verdict close to the malicious threshold deserves the same urgency as a confirmed malicious one.
investigation_steps: Review the sandbox's behavioral report for the specific triggering actions (macro execution, network calls, process spawning).
response_guidance: Treat high risk_score suspicious verdicts with the same urgency as FSB-001 pending manual review.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiSandbox Ransomware Classification
description: A submitted file's dynamic analysis behavior is classified specifically as ransomware (mass file encryption, ransom-note creation, shadow-copy deletion observed in the sandbox execution environment).
detection_logic: Filters FortiSandbox verdict log for ransomware-family classification.
spl:
index=fortisandbox sourcetype=fsb_verdict verdict="malicious" malware_family="*ransomware*"
| table _time, filename, file_hash, submitting_device, malware_family
tuning_guidance: No tuning — treat every occurrence as an emergency.
investigation_steps: Immediately trace the submission source and any recipient/endpoint that may have already received the file.
response_guidance: Treat as an active ransomware incident: isolate any host that may have received the file, and activate the organization's ransomware response plan.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact

author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiSandbox Detects Same Malware Hash Across Multiple Submissions
description: The same file hash is submitted to FortiSandbox multiple times from different source products or different users within a short window — consistent with a coordinated campaign delivering the same payload broadly across the organization via multiple channels.

data_sources.name: FortiSandbox verdict log
data_sources.description: Submission events with file hash and submitter.

detection_logic: Counts distinct submitters/submitting devices per file hash in a rolling window.
spl:
index=fortisandbox sourcetype=fsb_verdict
| bin _time span=6h
| stats dc(submitting_device) as distinct_submitters, values(submitting_device) as submitters by file_hash, verdict, _time
| where distinct_submitters>=3
tuning_guidance: Common commodity malware/spam campaigns generate this pattern routinely — cross-reference against known outbreak advisories.
investigation_steps: Identify the common delivery vector across submitters.
Sweep for the hash across FortiEDR/FortiClient endpoint telemetry.
response_guidance: Block the hash organization-wide via connector integrations where available; contain the common delivery source.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiSandbox Evasion Technique Detected During Analysis
description: FortiSandbox's own telemetry flags anti-analysis/sandbox-evasion behavior in a submitted file (VM/sandbox detection checks, execution delays, environment fingerprinting) even when the file does not otherwise trigger a definitive malicious verdict. Sandbox-aware malware deliberately behaving differently under analysis is itself a signal worth tracking, since it may result in an under-confident verdict for a file that is actually malicious.

data_sources.name: FortiSandbox verdict log
data_sources.description: Anti-analysis/evasion indicators observed during dynamic analysis.

detection_logic: Filters FortiSandbox verdict log for files flagged with evasion-technique indicators regardless of final verdict.
spl:
index=fortisandbox sourcetype=fsb_verdict evasion_detected="true"
| table _time, filename, file_hash, verdict, evasion_indicators, submitting_device
tuning_guidance: Treat as an enrichment signal that raises confidence on an otherwise-ambiguous verdict, not a standalone alert.
investigation_steps: Manually review files with evasion indicators but a non-malicious verdict, especially if submitted from a high-value delivery channel (executive mailbox, Internet-facing upload form).
response_guidance: Escalate for manual analysis if the verdict is inconclusive despite evasion indicators being present.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiSandbox Malicious Verdict Followed by FortiGate C2 Connection
