description: A file submitted for sandboxing returns a malicious verdict, and the identified C2 infrastructure from the sandbox report (or a host that received the file) is subsequently observed connecting outbound through FortiGate — closing the loop from file-level detection to confirmed network-level compromise. One of the Security Fabric correlation chains the master specification calls out by name.

data_sources.name: FortiSandbox verdict + FortiGate traffic log
data_sources.description: Malicious verdict cross-referenced with subsequent traffic to the sandbox-identified C2 indicators or from the file's delivery target.

detection_logic: Correlates a FortiSandbox malicious verdict's extracted C2 IOCs with subsequent FortiGate traffic-log connections matching those indicators.
spl:
index=fortisandbox sourcetype=fsb_verdict verdict="malicious"
| eval stage="1_malicious_verdict"
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound"
  | lookup fsb_c2_iocs.csv dstip OUTPUT is_sandbox_c2
  | where is_sandbox_c2="true"
  | eval stage="2_c2_connection" ]
| transaction file_hash maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_malicious_verdict")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, file_hash, dstip, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires the sandbox's extracted network IOCs to be published to a lookup (fsb_c2_iocs.csv) consumable by the FortiGate-side search — validate this pipeline exists in your deployment before relying on it.
investigation_steps: Identify the internal host that connected to the C2 indicator.
Treat as a confirmed active compromise.
response_guidance: Isolate the affected host immediately and initiate incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: malicious sandbox verdict -> traffic to sandbox-extracted C2 indicator

title: Fortinet Administrator Credential Compromise Escalates to Fleet-Wide Policy Change
description: A brute-force/spray-derived administrator compromise on a single FortiGate (FGT-004) or on FortiManager itself (FMG-004) is followed by a policy-package change on FortiManager and installation to multiple downstream devices. This is the master, Security-Fabric-wide version of the pattern FGT-020/FGT-039 detect at a single-device level: it confirms the same compromised identity was subsequently used to reach fleet-wide configuration authority, not just one device.

data_sources.name: FortiGate + FortiManager event logs
data_sources.description: Admin compromise indicator on either product correlated with a subsequent FortiManager policy-package install.

detection_logic: Correlates a successful-login-after-failures event (FGT-004/FMG-004 pattern) for a given administrator identity with a subsequent FortiManager policy install action attributed to the same identity, within 60 minutes.
spl:
index=fortinet OR index=fortimanager
| eval stage=case(sourcetype="fgt_event" AND action="login" AND status="success","1_admin_compromised", sourcetype="fmg_event" AND action="login" AND status="success","1_admin_compromised", sourcetype="fmg_event" AND msg="*install*","2_fleet_push", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=60m startswith=eval(stage="1_admin_compromised")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, srcip, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires the same-identity assumption to hold across both products' authentication systems (i.e. shared administrator accounts or a mapped identity) — validate your organization's admin-account model before relying on the user-field join.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live fleet-wide incident.
Identify every device the subsequent install affected.
Audit every configuration change made across the fleet since the compromised login.
response_guidance: Suspend the compromised identity across both platforms, halt further deployments, and prepare to roll back every affected FortiGate to its known-good configuration.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: admin compromise (FortiGate or FortiManager) -> FortiManager fleet policy install, same identity

title: VPN Credential Compromise Leads to Internal Reconnaissance and Lateral Movement
description: The master VPN-compromise attack chain named explicitly in the specification: VPN authentication failures, followed by a success (FGT-054), followed by internal network reconnaissance (FGT-058), followed by RDP/SMB/SSH connections to multiple internal hosts (FGT-059). Presented here as a single named, multi-stage correlation for dashboards/reporting purposes on top of the individual atomic/sequence detections that compose it.

data_sources.name: FortiGate VPN + traffic logs
data_sources.description: Full VPN authentication and subsequent internal traffic timeline for a single user/session.

detection_logic: A four-stage transaction spanning VPN brute force, successful login, internal scanning, and multi-host RDP/SMB/SSH connections for the same VPN-assigned identity within a 90-minute window.
spl:
index=fortinet
| eval stage=case(subtype="vpn" AND action="ssl-login-fail","1_vpn_failures", subtype="vpn" AND action="ssl-login","2_vpn_success", subtype="forward" AND dc_dstip_flag=1,"3_recon", subtype="forward" AND (service="RDP" OR service="SMB" OR dstport=22),"4_lateral_movement", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=90m startswith=eval(stage="1_vpn_failures")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, user, srcip, stage
tuning_guidance: This is a reporting/dashboard rollup of FGT-052/054/058/059 — implement each underlying detection first and treat this as a derived view rather than a new independent search to maintain.
investigation_steps: Pull the full timeline from initial VPN failure through lateral movement for the incident report.
Identify every internal host touched during the reconnaissance and lateral-movement stages.
response_guidance: Disconnect the VPN session, disable the account, and isolate every touched internal host; treat as a confirmed, multi-stage intrusion.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1046: Network Service Discovery
MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: VPN failures -> success -> internal recon -> RDP/SMB/SSH to multiple hosts

title: FortiManager Compromise Reaches Fleet-Wide Impact via Script or Policy Deployment
description: The named FortiManager Fleet Attack chain from the specification: a FortiManager administrator compromise (FMG-004), followed by either a policy-package modification/install (FMG-013/014/015) or a CLI script created and run across multiple devices (FMG-017/018/019), affecting the managed fleet. This is the single highest-consequence chain in the entire Fortinet catalogue given FortiManager's blast radius.

data_sources.name: FortiManager event log
data_sources.description: Full session timeline from compromised login through fleet-wide action.

detection_logic: A three-stage transaction: admin compromise, followed by either a policy install or script execution, with a target device_count above the fleet-wide threshold, within 60 minutes.
spl:
index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event
| eval stage=case(action="login" AND status="success","1_admin_compromised", msg="*install*" OR (msg="*script*" AND msg="*run*"),"2_fleet_action", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=60m startswith=eval(stage="1_admin_compromised")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, srcip, stage
tuning_guidance: Same identity-join caveat as FNT-X-001; requires the FMG-004 compromise pattern to precede the fleet action within the correlation window to avoid over-matching routine legitimate deployments.
investigation_steps: Treat as the highest-priority live incident this catalogue can raise.
Identify every affected device and exactly what was changed/executed on each.
Preserve FortiAnalyzer logs immediately given the risk of a follow-on log-destruction step (FNT-X-010).
response_guidance: Suspend the FortiManager account, halt all pending deployments, and begin fleet-wide rollback to known-good configuration; this should trigger the organization's highest-severity incident response tier.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter
MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: FortiManager admin compromise -> fleet-wide policy install or script execution

title: FortiMail Phishing Reaches Endpoint Execution and FortiGate Command-and-Control
description: The named Security Fabric chain: a phishing/malware email delivered by FortiMail (FML-002/003) to a recipient, followed by a malicious-process or malware detection on that same recipient's endpoint via FortiClient/EMS (EMS-006), followed by that endpoint generating an outbound C2-pattern connection through FortiGate (FGT-072/083). Ties email delivery, endpoint execution, and network C2 into a single incident timeline.

data_sources.name: FortiMail + EMS + FortiGate logs
data_sources.path: history log; endpoint AV events; traffic/IPS logs
data_sources.description: Delivered malicious email correlated with endpoint malware detection and subsequent network C2 activity for the same recipient/host.

detection_logic: Joins a delivered phishing/malware email (recipient mailbox) to a malware/malicious-process detection on the corresponding endpoint (via a user-to-hostname mapping lookup), then to a subsequent outbound C2-pattern connection from that same host, within a 24-hour window.
spl:
index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history (disposition="phishing" OR disposition="malware") action="delivered"
| lookup user_to_hostname.csv to OUTPUT hostname
| eval stage="1_phishing_delivered"
| append [ search index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event msg="*malware*detect*" | eval stage="2_endpoint_execution" ]
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=ips OR (sourcetype=fgt_traffic AND direction="outbound")
  | lookup fgt_dest_baseline.csv srcip dstip OUTPUT is_known | where isnull(is_known) | eval stage="3_network_c2" ]
| transaction hostname maxspan=24h startswith=eval(stage="1_phishing_delivered")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, hostname, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained user-to-hostname mapping (from EMS's own device registration data) to join the mail and endpoint domains — the single largest implementation dependency in this correlation.
investigation_steps: Reconstruct the full timeline from delivery through network C2.
Isolate the endpoint and block the C2 destination immediately.
response_guidance: Isolate the endpoint, block the C2 indicator fleet-wide, and force credential rotation for the affected user given the likelihood of credential theft alongside execution.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: phishing delivered -> endpoint malware execution -> network C2 from same host

title: Exploit or Malware Execution Leads to Confirmed Network Beaconing
description: An IPS exploit hit or antivirus-allowed malware detection against a host is followed by that host establishing a beaconing pattern (FGT-072) or a FortiEDR-confirmed network C2 block (FEDR-008) — combining network- and endpoint-side C2 confirmation into a single higher-confidence finding than either signal alone.

data_sources.name: FortiGate IPS/AV + FortiEDR logs
data_sources.description: Initial compromise indicator correlated with subsequent beaconing/C2 confirmation for the same host.

detection_logic: Correlates an IPS exploit hit or allowed-malware detection against a host with a subsequent beaconing pattern or FortiEDR C2 block from that same host within 6 hours.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm (type=utm subtype=ips) OR (type=utm subtype=virus action=allowed)
| eval victim=dstip, stage="1_initial_compromise"
| append [ search index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event event_type="network" classification="c2" | eval victim=hostname, stage="2_confirmed_c2" ]
| transaction victim maxspan=6h startswith=eval(stage="1_initial_compromise")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, victim, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a hostname-to-IP mapping to join the network (IP-keyed) and endpoint (hostname-keyed) domains — maintain via DHCP lease/asset-inventory lookup.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed compromise given the two independent corroborating signals.
Isolate the host immediately.
response_guidance: Isolate the host, block the C2 destination, and initiate incident response with high confidence given the dual network+endpoint confirmation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: IPS/AV compromise indicator -> confirmed beaconing/C2, same host

title: Same Malware Hash Observed Across FortiGate, FortiClient, and FortiMail
description: The same file hash is detected across two or more distinct product telemetry sources (FortiGate antivirus, FortiClient/EMS endpoint detection, FortiMail attachment scanning) — confirming a single campaign is reaching the organization through multiple delivery vectors simultaneously, which changes the response posture from single-host remediation to organization-wide hunting and blocking.

data_sources.name: FortiGate + EMS + FortiMail logs
data_sources.path: type=utm subtype=virus; endpoint AV events; email history log
data_sources.description: File hash detections across three independent Fortinet telemetry sources.

detection_logic: Unions malware/virus-name detections across the three product sourcetypes and counts distinct source products per detected name/hash within a 24-hour window.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_utm type=utm subtype=virus
| eval source_product="FortiGate"
| append [ search index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event msg="*malware*detect*" | eval source_product="FortiClient" ]
| append [ search index=fortimail sourcetype=fml_history disposition="malware" | eval source_product="FortiMail", virus=virus_name ]
| bin _time span=24h
| stats dc(source_product) as distinct_products, values(source_product) as products by virus, _time
| where distinct_products>=2
tuning_guidance: Requires consistent malware-naming across products (FortiGuard's own naming is generally consistent, but validate against real detections in your environment); consider joining on file_hash instead of virus name where available for higher precision.
investigation_steps: Identify every host/mailbox/connection the hash was seen on across all three products.
Determine the common delivery source or campaign infrastructure.
response_guidance: Treat as an organization-wide campaign: block the hash and delivery infrastructure across all products, and sweep all endpoints for the indicator.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: FortiWeb Exploit Reaches FortiGate Network Connection and FortiEDR Endpoint Compromise
description: The first named Security Fabric chain in the specification: a FortiWeb exploit hit against a protected web application (FWB-001/003/007), followed by the backend application server generating an unusual outbound FortiGate connection (FWB-013), followed by a FortiEDR malicious-process detection on that same server if endpoint agents are deployed on the application tier. Chains the web, network, and endpoint layers into a single incident for application servers with full Security Fabric coverage.

data_sources.name: FortiWeb + FortiGate + FortiEDR logs
data_sources.path: attack log; type=traffic subtype=forward; process events
data_sources.description: Web exploit correlated through network connection to endpoint process detection on the same backend server.

detection_logic: Three-stage transaction: WAF exploit hit against a known application, mapped to its backend IP, correlated with a subsequent new outbound connection from that IP, correlated with a subsequent FortiEDR malicious-process detection on the corresponding hostname.
spl:
index=fortiweb sourcetype=fwb_attack severity="critical"
| lookup fwb_backend_ips.csv http_host OUTPUT backend_ip
| eval stage="1_web_exploit", key=backend_ip
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound"
  | lookup fgt_dest_baseline.csv srcip dstip OUTPUT is_known | where isnull(is_known)
  | eval stage="2_network_connection", key=srcip ]
| append [ search index=fortiedr sourcetype=fedr_event classification="malicious"
  | lookup ip_to_hostname.csv hostname OUTPUT ip | eval stage="3_endpoint_compromise", key=ip ]
| transaction key maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_web_exploit")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, key, stage
tuning_guidance: The three-way join requires backend-IP-to-hostname mapping in addition to the web-app-to-backend-IP mapping used in FWB-013 — this is the most implementation-heavy correlation in the catalogue and should be validated stage-by-stage before enabling end-to-end.
investigation_steps: Reconstruct the full attack timeline across all three products.
Treat the application server as compromised at whatever stage was confirmed.
response_guidance: Isolate the application server, patch the exploited vulnerability, and conduct a full forensic review given confirmed multi-layer compromise.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: WAF exploit -> new outbound connection -> endpoint malicious-process detection, same server

title: FortiAuthenticator Identity Compromise Reaches VPN Access and Internal Reconnaissance
description: The named identity-compromise chain from the specification: a FortiAuthenticator token/identity change (FAC-004/005) is followed by a successful VPN authentication for the affected identity (FGT-054), followed by internal network reconnaissance from that VPN session (FGT-058). Extends FAC-005's two-stage correlation one step further into the network layer.

data_sources.name: FortiAuthenticator + FortiGate logs
data_sources.path: identity/token change events; VPN authentication; traffic log
data_sources.description: Identity change correlated through VPN authentication to subsequent internal reconnaissance.

detection_logic: Three-stage transaction: FortiAuthenticator identity/token change, subsequent VPN authentication success for the same identity, subsequent internal reconnaissance traffic from the VPN-assigned address, within 60 minutes.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event msg="*token*" (msg="*reassign*" OR msg="*creat*")
| eval stage="1_identity_change"
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=vpn action="ssl-login" | eval stage="2_vpn_auth" ]
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward
  | lookup fgt_vpn_pools.csv srcip OUTPUT is_vpn_pool | where is_vpn_pool="true"
  | stats dc(dstip) as distinct_dests by srcip, user | where distinct_dests>=20 | eval stage="3_recon" ]
| transaction user maxspan=60m startswith=eval(stage="1_identity_change")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Same legitimate-token-replacement caveat as FAC-005 — cross-reference against help-desk tickets before escalating to Critical.
investigation_steps: Verify the identity change against a change/help-desk ticket.
Trace the reconnaissance traffic for follow-on targeted connections.
response_guidance: Disconnect the VPN session, revert the identity change, and force credential/token re-enrollment; treat as a confirmed identity-infrastructure compromise.

title: FortiSandbox Malicious Verdict Confirmed by Matching Endpoint and Network Detections
description: The named FortiSandbox correlation chain from the specification: a malicious file verdict (FSB-001) is confirmed by a matching hash detection on an endpoint (EMS-006) and/or the sandbox's extracted C2 indicators appearing in subsequent FortiGate traffic (FSB-006). Presented as the unified three-way confirmation view combining file-level, endpoint-level, and network-level evidence for the same campaign.

data_sources.name: FortiSandbox + EMS + FortiGate logs
data_sources.path: verdict events; endpoint AV events; traffic log
data_sources.description: Sandbox verdict cross-referenced with endpoint hash matches and network C2 indicator matches.

detection_logic: Correlates a FortiSandbox malicious verdict's file_hash with subsequent EMS endpoint detections of the same hash and/or FortiGate traffic to the sandbox's extracted C2 indicators, within 24 hours.
spl:
index=fortisandbox sourcetype=fsb_verdict verdict="malicious"
| eval stage="1_sandbox_verdict"
| append [ search index=forticlient_ems sourcetype=ems_event msg="*malware*detect*" | eval stage="2_endpoint_match" ]
| append [ search index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_traffic type=traffic subtype=forward direction="outbound"
  | lookup fsb_c2_iocs.csv dstip OUTPUT is_sandbox_c2 | where is_sandbox_c2="true" | eval stage="3_network_c2" ]
| transaction file_hash maxspan=24h startswith=eval(stage="1_sandbox_verdict")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, file_hash, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires both the endpoint (hash-keyed) and network (IOC-lookup-keyed) join paths to be populated from the sandbox's own report data — validate both pipelines independently.
investigation_steps: Confirm which stages matched and reconstruct the full campaign timeline.
Sweep the full endpoint fleet for the confirmed hash.
response_guidance: Block the hash and C2 indicators fleet-wide; isolate every confirmed-affected endpoint.

title: Coordinated Defense-Control Impairment Across the Fortinet Fleet
description: Defense-control weakening events occur across two or more distinct Fortinet products within a short window — e.g. logging disabled on multiple FortiGates (FGT-040/042) coinciding with a FortiManager fleet-wide security-control-removing deployment (FMG-015) and/or FortiAnalyzer log deletion (FAZ-005). Individually any one of these is already a Critical-severity finding; their co-occurrence across products is the strongest possible signal that an attacker is deliberately blinding the organization's entire Fortinet-based detection capability ahead of a larger operation.

data_sources.name: FortiGate + FortiManager + FortiAnalyzer event logs
data_sources.description: Defense-control-weakening events across the Security Fabric within a correlation window.

detection_logic: Unions defense-impairment-classified events (logging disabled, security profile removed, fleet-wide control-weakening install, log purge) across FortiGate, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer sourcetypes and flags any 60-minute window with events from two or more distinct products.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event (cfgpath="log.*" OR cfgpath="ips.sensor" OR cfgpath="antivirus.profile") action="Delete" OR cfgattr="status"
| eval source_product="FortiGate", stage="control_weakened"
| append [ search index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event msg="*policy package*" msg="*remov*" | eval source_product="FortiManager", stage="control_weakened" ]
| append [ search index=fortianalyzer sourcetype=faz_event (msg="*log*delet*" OR msg="*log*purg*") | eval source_product="FortiAnalyzer", stage="control_weakened" ]
| bin _time span=60m
| stats dc(source_product) as distinct_products, values(source_product) as products, values(user) as users by _time
| where distinct_products>=2
tuning_guidance: Rare, high-value alert by design — expect near-zero legitimate occurrences; any hit warrants immediate all-hands review regardless of individual event confidence.
investigation_steps: Treat as the highest-priority incident this catalogue can raise.
Reconstruct every defense-control change across all three products in the window.
Preserve any remaining logs immediately.
response_guidance: Activate full incident response: isolate management access to all three platforms, restore every weakened control, and assume the entire fleet requires configuration verification against known-good baselines.

title: FortiAuthenticator Identity Compromise Reaches FortiManager Administrative Access
description: Tier-0 identity infrastructure (FortiAuthenticator) compromise reaching Tier-0 management infrastructure (FortiManager) — a token/identity change or new-administrator event on FortiAuthenticator (FAC-004/007) followed by a FortiManager administrative login for a corresponding identity. Represents the worst-case cross-infrastructure scenario: an attacker who controls identity issuance can potentially mint valid credentials for the platform that controls the entire firewall fleet.

data_sources.name: FortiAuthenticator + FortiManager logs
data_sources.path: identity/token change events; FortiManager login events
data_sources.description: Identity-infrastructure change correlated with subsequent FortiManager administrative access.

detection_logic: Correlates a FortiAuthenticator identity/administrator change with a subsequent FortiManager login for a related identity within 60 minutes — the identity relationship may require an explicit mapping lookup if FortiManager does not share FortiAuthenticator's namespace directly.
spl:
index=fortiauthenticator sourcetype=fac_event msg="*admin*" (msg="*creat*" OR msg="*token*")
| eval stage="1_identity_infra_change"
| append [ search index=fortimanager sourcetype=fmg_event action="login" status="success" | eval stage="2_fmg_access" ]
| transaction user maxspan=60m startswith=eval(stage="1_identity_infra_change")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, srcip, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained identity mapping between FortiAuthenticator principals and FortiManager administrator accounts if they are not the same directory-backed identity — validate this join is meaningful in your environment before enabling as a paging alert.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident spanning both identity and management infrastructure.
Suspend both the FortiAuthenticator and FortiManager sessions pending investigation.
response_guidance: Suspend affected identities across both platforms; audit all FortiManager activity since the FortiAuthenticator change.

title: Post-Exploitation Fleet Reconnaissance Following Suspected Fortinet Vulnerability Exploitation
description: This detection does not claim to identify exploitation of a specific Fortinet CVE directly — FortiGate/FortiManager telemetry frequently cannot observe the exploit primitive itself (e.g. an authentication-bypass or memory-corruption vulnerability reached via a crafted HTTP request to the management interface may not generate a distinguishing log event). Instead it looks for the *post-exploitation* behaviors real Fortinet-targeting campaigns have exhibited after gaining unauthorized access: unexplained administrative-interface activity immediately followed by system information gathering (`get system status`, `diagnose` commands) and new local-account creation, without a preceding normal login pattern. Treat this as a low-confidence hunting search, not a precision alert.

data_sources.name: FortiGate event log
data_sources.description: Administrative CLI/API command activity and account-creation events, without a corresponding expected authentication pattern.

detection_logic: Flags a system-information-gathering command sequence immediately followed by local account creation, where the acting session does not match a known-good administrator baseline — a coarse behavioral proxy for post-exploitation activity rather than a signature for any specific vulnerability.
spl:
index=fortinet sourcetype=fgt_event type=event subtype=system
| eval stage=case(msg="*get system status*" OR msg="*diagnose*","1_recon", cfgpath="system.admin" AND action="Add","2_new_account", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction srcip maxspan=15m startswith=eval(stage="1_recon")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| lookup fgt_admin_ip_baseline.csv srcip OUTPUT is_known_admin_source
| where isnull(is_known_admin_source)
| table _time, srcip, user, stage
tuning_guidance: High false-positive potential given the coarse behavioral proxy — this is explicitly a hunting search for use during a declared Fortinet vulnerability advisory window (e.g. after a PSIRT disclosure affecting your deployed version), not a standing production alert. Do not claim this detects a specific CVE.
investigation_steps: Cross-reference the source IP against current Fortinet PSIRT advisories and your patch level for the affected product.
Manually review the full command sequence and any account created.
Check FortiGuard/vendor IOC feeds for indicators matching your version.
response_guidance: If a matching, currently-unpatched CVE exists for your deployed version, treat as a probable compromise: patch immediately, audit the account roster, and consider the device compromised pending forensic review.
